voices-from-global-green.name: Voices from Global Green
voices-from-global-green.bio: Meet some of the artists and activists from Global Green as they share stories from the frontlines of change - from ecological restoration to creative resistance.

marko.name: MarkO
marko.bio: MarkO blends Irish folk tradition with shamanic and atmospheric soundscapes to create deep connection and reflection. Inspired by nature and ancient storytelling, their music uses voice and melody to offer an uplifting, grounding experience that transcends genre. Whether in intimate settings or on festival stages, MarkO’s performances aim to touch the heart, awaken emotion, and leave audiences feeling moved and renewed through soulful, intuitive expression.

the-savage-jim-breen.name: The Savage Jim Breen
the-savage-jim-breen.bio: The Savage Jim Breen are an Irish alt-folk band formed in 2012, though its members, James Haughey, Greg Breen, James Savage and Manus Crowley, have been playing together in various forms for many years. Their music offers a rare blend of original songwriting, uplifting harmonies and folk-rooted storytelling, capturing something of life in 21st-century Ireland: its pressures, contradictions, humour, hope and humanity. With multiple songwriters in the band, their sound shifts through folk, roots and alternative landscapes from one song to the next, while still holding a distinctive shared voice. By their own admission, all songs are translated through a single gaze, that of the mysterious figure known as the Savage Jim Breen

luke-clerkin.name: Luke Clerkin
luke-clerkin.bio: Luke Clerkin is a two-time Sports and Cultural Council songwriting competition winner from Tallaght. He has performed at festivals and venues all over Ireland and abroad including in Germany, Londonkelsey, LA and Bulgaria. His songs have received airplay on RTÉ Radio One, BBC Northern Ireland, Spin 1038, Spin South West, KCLR, FM104, and Today FM, among others. Luke released his debut album 'Orpheus' to critical acclaim in January 2025

riddim-and-ting.name: Riddim and Ting
riddim-and-ting.bio: West of Ireland duo Riddim & Ting bring reggae soundsystem culture to Global Green, blending reggae, dub, dancehall, ska, jungle and DnB into an irresistible dancefloor journey. Working in the classic reggae soundsystem style of DJ juggling the riddims and live MC laying down her own unique take, their goal is to nice up the place and put a smile on your face…yes now!

raggapuffin.name: Raggapuffin
raggapuffin.bio: Dynamic booty rave merchants full of bass and sass. Big baselines and all kinda beats - baile funk, dancehall, tropical techno - via DJ Kelsey Sheridan; vocals and antics via the incomparable Lady Grew, electric and live drums extravaganza via Iarla Fox. Expect raucous festival party vibes, with live elements, guests and mad vibes.

dj-ruari-santiago-mcbride-and-ollie-moor.name: DJ Ruari-Santiago McBride and Ollie Moore
dj-ruari-santiago-mcbride-and-ollie-moor.bio: Dancehall and beaty tropical vibes for the floor. From Colombian to the Caribbean, all over Turtle Island, and over to West Africa too, these tunes are made for dancing. Bringing beats and glitches, organica and electronica, kicks and groves together in a way that grabs, jolts and shakes the floor! Regulars at their own Eats and Beats events in Cloughjordan, and at festivals and quirky cosy things all over, expect to get up to get down.

dj-kelsey.name: DJ Kelsey
dj-kelsey.bio: DJ Kelsey's sets are a vibrant fusion of global sounds, techy rollers, and baile and dembow riddims, all wrapped in bass-driven beauty. Expect high energy and a lot of booty from this one on the dancefloor.

dj-aaronoscar.name: DJ Aaronoscar
dj-aaronoscar.bio: Weaving warm sets with worldwide bass wobbles and beautiful melodies to move you! Recent sets set the scene with transcendent electronics (melodic house/techno, EDM with meltingly velvet vocals), or ground stomping earthy-hard drops (DnB, electro-swing, and glitch-hop)

dj-eli.name: DJ Eli
dj-eli.bio: California born, Donegal based, Eli is an enthusiast of contemporary psychedelic techno and aims to create a hypnotising atmosphere that invites people to dance themselves out of their heads and into their bodies. For the last 10 years Eli has been exploring different sounds and genres through his dj sets but has always found techno closest to his heart.

morning-yoga.name: Morning Yoga
morning-yoga.bio: Shake off that fuzzy festival head, wake up your body and get your energy flowing with Majella O’Connor. No experience needed. Just bring yourself (and a mat if you have one). Come early as this is popular. Leave feeling relaxed, centered and ready for the day ahead

laura-kehoe.name: Laura Kehoe
laura-kehoe.bio: Join Dr. Laura Kehoe for a joyful protest singing workshop. Learn powerful songs of resistance and solidarity, then belt them out with kindred souls - no experience needed, just bring your lungs and your spirit.

feeding-ourselves-food-system-transforma.name: Feeding Ourselves - Food System Transformation with Siolta Croí
feeding-ourselves-food-system-transforma.bio: A panel discussion facilitated by Cultivate's Davie Philip with Siolta Croi, Talamh Beo and more from our global green community, exploring the potential of local food economies and innovative approaches to reshape the wider agri-food system - as if people and planet mattered. Agroecology, food sovereignty, and a whole lot more.

decolonising-agriculture-with-rupa-marya.name: Decolonising Agriculture with Rupa Marya and Ollie Moore
decolonising-agriculture-with-rupa-marya.bio: Ollie Moore and Rupa Marya in conversation hosted by Joanne Fullerton of Siolta Croí. What happens when we peel back the layers of colonisation and begin anew, with fresh eyes, at our land, our farming and our food? What can we learn from the past and from our speculative futures via time travelling and imagination? Join us on this journey.

young-voices-of-africa.name: Young Voices of Africa
young-voices-of-africa.bio: An all-singing, all-dancing, emotionally charged performance from Young Voices of Africa - a diverse and dynamic group of young people from across the African continent and diaspora, raising their voices on the issues affecting their communities and the wider continent

caoimhe-butterly-and-rupa-marya-in-conve.name: Caoimhe Butterly and Rupa Marya in Conversation: Palestine - what next?
caoimhe-butterly-and-rupa-marya-in-conve.bio: Caoimhe Butterly Caoimhe Butterly is a human rights activist, educator, documentary filmmaker & trauma-informed psychotherapist. She has worked as a volunteer ambulance worker in Gaza, alongside Palestinian paramedics, and has also spent years in the West Bank. She has worked with refugee and displaced communities for over 25 years in Palestine, Iraq, Lebanon, Syria, Mexico, Guatemala, Haiti, Ukraine, Greece, Calais and elsewhere & currently works in psychosocial and trauma support work, with humanitarian and frontline responders. Caoimhe has been involved in flotillas to break the siege of Gaza since 2008, including sailing with the most recent Global Sumud Flotilla, as part of an onboard mental health supports team. Rupa Marya is a physician, activist, writer, mother, soil lover and composer. She was Professor of Medicine at the University of California, San Francisco, practicing and teaching hospital medicine for 23 years until she was fired in May 2025 for her advocacy of Palestinian life and liberation. Now in Ireland her work focuses on food sovereignty, community health and decolonial practice.

leen-maarouf.name: Leen Maarouf
leen-maarouf.bio: Palestinian-Lebenese singer with a spell-binding voice. Leen Maarouf is a multi-talented Palestinian singer/songwriter from Lebanon who uses art to craft her unique story and views on the world. With insightful lyrics and powerful vocals Leen has delighted huge audiences at protests, festivals and gigs all over Ireland. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session.

palestine-what-now-what-next-in-ireland.name: Palestine - what now, what next in Ireland?
palestine-what-now-what-next-in-ireland.bio: Taking action: stop the game, stop the occupation, stop colonisation. With Irish Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Belfast BDS, Mothers Against Genocide Neart Nur and more. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session.

abood-aladham.name: Abood Aladham
abood-aladham.bio: Abood Aladham is a Palestinian Jordanian multifaceted artist and activist. A champion, dexterous, playful beatboxer, this cheeky chappie also uses looping and other elements to bring you on an amazing and unexpected journey. Abood has pioneered Jordanian beatboxing and is the founder of the Jordan beatboxing championship. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session

yalla-craic-play-roots-and-resilience.name: Yalla Craic - Play Roots and Resilience
yalla-craic-play-roots-and-resilience.bio: Yalla Craic is a cultural and educational game development studio that creates engaging learning experiences designed to bring people together across cultures. Roots and Resistance, is a unique trilingual card game: Irish, Arabic, and English. The game offers four different games in a single deck, providing players with multiple ways to explore and engage with the shared histories, cultures, struggles, and resilience of Ireland and Palestine. Through storytelling, memory challenges, creative connections, and discussion-based activities, players discover common values and experiences while developing a deeper appreciation for both cultures. Designed for young people and adults, Roots and Resistance transforms learning into an interactive and enjoyable experience that inspires curiosity, empathy, and meaningful conversations. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session.

r-o-shea.name: Rú O'Shea
r-o-shea.bio: is an Offaly-born, Dublin-based folk musician and multi-instrumentalist. Known for playing guitar, mandolin, bouzouki, and banjo, he blends traditional Irish folk with original songs and is an advocate for the healing and community-building power of live music. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session.

the-shan-vans.name: The Shan Vans
the-shan-vans.bio: A West Belfast band pulling from post-punk tension, Irish- language revival, and heavy, atmosphere-driven guitar music. Rooted in the streets and memory of their fractured city, the band make songs that move between place, history, and mythology.

robot-rock.name: Robot Rock
robot-rock.bio: Evolving from their roots as a live dance anthem band, RobotRock is bringing a new chapter to Electric Picnic 2026. Stepping out of the mash-up realm, the band now performs their own tent-shaking original beats. Heavily influenced by big beat era dance music, RobotRock's fresh sound channels the floor-filling energy of pioneers like The Chemical Brothers, Daft Punk, Underworld, and Fatboy Slim. Expect the same massive, live experience that has captivated festivals, clubs, and venues across the country, now fueled by hard-hitting, synth-driven original tracks.

sauti-club-cork.name: Sauti Club Cork
sauti-club-cork.bio: Artists Cliff Mashetti and Raphael Olympio, founders of Sauti Studios in Cork, use poetry, spoken word, music, and storytelling to explore identity, belonging, and social justice. Through powerful performances and creative expression, they challenge racism in Ireland while celebrating resilience, diversity, and the power of community.

hip-hop-hooray-dj-rosko.name: Hip Hop Hooray & DJ Rosko
hip-hop-hooray-dj-rosko.bio: The HIP HOP HOORAY party makes a welcome return to Global Green this year for a late night celebration of the golden age of hip hop. Expect 90's hip hop classics and a party atmosphere all expertly mixed by DJ Rosko with Reo Oderile on live drums and guest MC's.

hlymrekr.name: Hlymrekr
hlymrekr.bio: Hlymrekr is a Limerick based club night and collective led by friends Eamonn Walsh and Ethan Madden. Limerick has a small but very rich music scene and they have carved out a notable space as an underground force built for the love of the dance. Hlymrekr, is a translation from Old Norse, meaning 'The Mighty Noise', and references the Viking's discovery of Limerick and the sound heard around The River Shannon. Eamo & ecat will shift between deep grooves, cosmic disco, percussive heat and beyond. Like their project's namesake, this sonic pairing promises to be mighty!

sophie-shaw.name: Sophie Shaw
sophie-shaw.bio: Sophie Shaw is a Belfast-based DJ and promoter whose sound is rooted in bass-driven music, drawing from techno, house and leftfield influences. With forward thinking selections and a sharp instinct for the dance-floor, she brings an energy that is deeply rooted in underground club culture. In 2024, Sophie founded Social Sounds, a Belfast-based event series that has quickly become a vital fixture in the city’s nightlife. Sophie’s musical passion and work reflects a deep commitment to underground music - both as a selector and a scene builder - making her a standout voice in Ireland’s new wave of club culture.

knum.name: KNUM
knum.bio: Cork based KNUM has been steadily contributing sets not only across Cork City but also across some of Ireland’s most renowned venues over the last number years, through his alias MUNK . Though originally rooted in groove-based techno as MUNK, his new style under KNUM has slowed down the pace and put focus on a wide-angle of genres, often weaving through house, prog-house, tech and even elements of trance. A rising star in Cork’s thriving musical landscape where the scene is forever pushing forward and driving towards its underground roots, KNUM represents the next generation of local innovators building on the city’s legacy of raw, boundary-pushing electronic culture.

b-r-e-d.name: B.R.E.D
b-r-e-d.bio: B.R.E.D has established himself as a dynamic force in the Irish electronic music scene. Having performed at Electric Picnic for the past number of years and Fuinneamh in 2024, he never fails to captivate audiences with his deep soundscapes which keep you on your toes. Each year, he has delivered sets that have kept crowds grooving until the early hours, no matter the day. Beyond the festival circuit, B.R.E.D has left his mark on the Irish music scene, having performed at well known venues and events across the country. From intimate club sets in Galway to outdoor gatherings in Cork, his sets never fail to impress. B.R.E.D's recent shift in sound has led him to exploring many new genres and the links found between them, so expect a set that leans on the experimental but relies on the groove.

pleasure-activism.name: Pleasure Activism
pleasure-activism.bio: Explore how joy, play, and movement can challenge systems of oppression and reimagine community spaces. This lively session invites you to get curious, get moving, and maybe get a little messy - all while seeing social justice through a lens of pleasure and access to third spaces. Expect paint splattering, wild body movement, and playful conversations. Bígí linn!

honouring-the-dexter-stories-heritage-wa.name: Honouring the Dexter – Stories, Heritage & Waste Not, Want Not
honouring-the-dexter-stories-heritage-wa.bio: A Local Green Box Cavan initiative - The Story of a Native Breed with Pauric Farrelly – exploring the heritage, resilience and importance of Dexter cattle within regenerative and local food systems. Waste Not, Want Not with Imelda Mullen – a practical and engaging demo showing how we can honour the whole animal: from transforming bones into nourishing broth to rendering fat into a natural skin cream, rooted in traditional thrift and circular living.

cultural-creatives-artivism-in-action.name: Cultural Creatives: Artivism in Action
cultural-creatives-artivism-in-action.bio: The Wellbeing Economy Alliance hosts a conversation with artists working at the intersection of ecology, social change, and degrowth. Together, they explore how creativity can deepen connection, provoke dialogue, challenge consumer culture, and inspire transformation towards more just and regenerative futures.

the-power-of-community.name: The Power of Community
the-power-of-community.bio: A panel discussion with activists from community-led housing, community energy, and community-supported agriculture exploring how people are coming together to meet real needs, share resources, and build more resilient local places. From neighbourhoods and food to renewable power, this conversation celebrates practical community action and the power of cooperation to shape a more resilient future.

mel-white-and-alys-taylor-s-spoken-word-.name: Mel White and Alys Taylor's Spoken Word Jam
mel-white-and-alys-taylor-s-spoken-word-.bio: Mel White is a multi-award winning spoken-word artist and seasoned festival performer based in Cloughjordan Ecovillage. Through her dynamic and moving spoken-word performance, Mel pokes fun at some of our social norms, highlights the very real need for change in response to global crises, and invites us to connect deeply to each other, and to what matters most to us....be prepared to laugh, and feel moved, connected, and inspired. Alys Taylor is a spontaneous spoken word wanderer, inspired by gifts of this earth, snails, the delight of mistakes, gorse flowers. She has a passionate love of broad beans, and well-baked potatoes, and an unwavering thirst for tea… Mel and Alys will be joined by other special guest performers for this festival special poetry jam.

anattapatrick.name: AnattaPatrick
anattapatrick.bio: AnattaPatrick crafts live multi-instrument looping sessions using voice, guitar, and a rich palette of atmospheric instruments. His performance weaves conscious songwriting, reflective stillness and upbeat danceable grooves. He invites the crowd into a shared space of celebration and Connection.

nat-stone.name: Nat Stone
nat-stone.bio: Nat Stone Nat’s story telling lyrics and raw, powerful soulful vocals, create an ambience of emotive journeying. Drawing on Americana, smoky jazz, murder balladry and folk, expect motifs of love and loss to fill the air with soaring sonority. Her first album The Old Salt Road was released in 2022 to critical acclaim.

sarah-szucs.name: Sarah Szucs
sarah-szucs.bio: Sarah Szucs draws from an eclectic mix of influences to create songs that blend sharp guitar work with candid, conversational lyrics. Expect biting observations, offbeat humour and unexpected sonic left turns

sol-chase.name: Sol Chase
sol-chase.bio: Sol is a multi-instrumentalist, songwriter, and musical facilitator from Colorado, currently residing in Tipperary. He has deep roots in the Bluegrass scene of the Rocky Mountains but has branched out into Jazz, Americana, and folk of all kinds. His songs speak to shared humanity, with messages of environmentalism, social activism, community building, and self exploration. Whether performing with his band Big Love Car Wash or as a solo artist, Sol creates heart-centred musical experiences that invite connection, participation, and belonging — weaving audiences into a shared space of joy, reflection, and community.

evergreen-choose-joy.name: Evergreen Choose-Joy
evergreen-choose-joy.bio: Evergreen is an Ireland-based cellist and singer-songwriter. Bending genres and genders, mixing ethnicities and artistic ethos, they deliver a dynamic sonic experience that reflects the experiences they have lived on this multitudinous planet. Originally hailing from Texas and China, Evergreen draws on traditions from western classical, global folk, jazz, and poetry to create music that is completely unique. Evergreen’s lyric work is rooted in a background of environmental sociology, presenting perspectives of greener living aligned with the Earth. Described as “inspired eclecticism” and “high-vibe folk”, Evergreen’s music “rejuvenates love and lust for life…[their music] is as accessible as oxygen, with no shortage of virtuosic flare” (KUTX, A&R Factory). Evergreen’s LP, Delicious Vignettes of Recent American Kind, can be found on all streaming platforms.

cloughjordan-candlelit-ensemble.name: Cloughjordan Candlelit Ensemble
cloughjordan-candlelit-ensemble.bio: An intimate collective of musicians based in and around Cloughjordan who gather twice each month in Cloughjordan Ecovillage to play, listen, and connect. This special performance offers a glimpse into the magic that emerges from those gatherings, as 13 musicians weave harmonies, melodies, and rhythms into a rich shared sound.

the-hqs.name: The HQs
the-hqs.bio: Dublin's foremost blood harmony and hillbilly funk outfit. Filling out the sonic space with sweet sweet and somehow big and booming harmonies. Americana, bluegrass, and more stringed and sonic wonderfulness.

the-accidental-rapper.name: The Accidental Rapper
the-accidental-rapper.bio: A finger on the pulse, engaged activist, the accidental rapper brings spoken word, hip hop vibes into a rabble rousing, people power place. Expect to join in and sing along to politically charged themes you never know could sound so damn good.

the-cazettes.name: The Cazettes
the-cazettes.bio: The Cazettes are a super-group of four friends who have come together to bring their favourite songs to life for your listening and dancing pleasure. They are known for playing an unexpected mix of bangers, everything from Fleetwood Mac to Eminem, Abba to Talking Heads to Dua Lipa - anything goes at a Party Set! It's all about the craic and having a great time - bring your good vibes, and get ready to have all the fun on the dancefloor!

dj-ollie-moore.name: DJ Ollie Moore
dj-ollie-moore.bio: DJ Ollie Moore From Dancehall to Cumbia, Tropical to Techno, and a sprinkling of mash-it-up-dj massive moments, expect organic electronica in all its glitchy quirked out depth .And somehow, this will sound like proper party music to let yourself go to. A regular at Cloughjordan's Eats and Beats and at festivals, events and shows all over. Check out his float notes series on mixcloud too.

anacalypsis.name: Anacalypsis
anacalypsis.bio: Conceptually this may go from collapse to calypso, but, mostly, this be bangin’ techno, from funky and bouncy to end-of-the-evening/world vibes. Party an Domhain ,so get on down to the last show in tow-in.

the-wednesday-gang.name: THE WEDNESDAY GANG
the-wednesday-gang.bio: The Wednesday Gang have been opening The Salty Dog Stage at The Electric Picnic since 2015. A seven piece act from Slane, Co. Meath that specialise in the art of the sing-song. With a sound that is based on Irish traditional music fused with American folk The Wednesday Gang have a quirky way of presenting covers by bands such as Edward Sharp, Elbow, Florence & The Machine etc. “Ramshackle rock n’roll at it’s best” The Irish Times

reluctant-bob-and-the-lonely-lovers.name: RELUCTANT BOB AND THE LONELY LOVERS
reluctant-bob-and-the-lonely-lovers.bio: Reluctant Bob & the Lonely Lovers, is a new project from songwriter & producer Robert Baker. With stellar support from the Lonely Lovers he constructs dreamy & melodic alternative pop - tinged with psychedelic influences Following support for debut single Dreamager across RTÉ Radio, BBC 6 Music, BBC Ulster, WFUV (NYC) and Triple R (AU) amongst others — and a Track of the Week nod from producer Steve Lillywhite (U2, Talking Heads, Morrissey) — the band continue to build towards their debut album release, due late 2026.

babyrat.name: BABYRAT
babyrat.bio: Bursting out of the heart of Cork City, BABYRAT is cutting through the noise with razor-sharp riffs, anthemic choruses and the kind of edge that power-pop has been missing. Their self-proclaimed ‘bitch-pop’ sound has sonically landed the bright-eyed five somewhere between The Strokes and Olivia Rodrigo, a sound which they have taken from local bars to arenas in just one year after forming in late 2024. BABYRAT delivers "an infectious energy with a confidence and chemistry that is unmatched" - Mia Tobin Power, University Express.

epilogue.name: EPILOGUE
epilogue.bio: Epilogue are an alt-rock/ post-punk band. The band launched their debut album 'Carousel' in late 2025. Exploring themes such as loss, dread and existential angst, the band got their start with this carnival inspired rock anthology. Taking inspiration from artists such as Radiohead, The Cure and Joy Division, the band would take a softer approach with their newer works releasing later this year. Forest Fest, Pop-monument and Ones to Watch in Whelan's are just a few live events featuring Epilogue this year. 2026 is shaping up to be a bright year for the band.

ria-rua.name: RIA RUA
ria-rua.bio: Ria Rua (“Red Queen” in Irish) is known for her explosive and emotional performances. Her lyrics are pointed and personal but the themes are universal: sex, power and freedom. Expect grungy and electronic rock anthems – a dynamic fusion of electronic pulses, grunge undertones, and alternative embellishments. Some sound like a helicopter crashing into a petrol station. Some have two drummers. All of them are driven by a single minded vision and urgency.

the-wran.name: THE WRAN
the-wran.bio: Hailing from the Comeragh Mountains of County Waterford, The Wran are four brothers: Tommy, Danny, Seán and Stephen Dunford. They bring a fresh voice to Irish music, blending trad with punk and a hint of psychedelia to create music that feels both timeless and new. Drawing inspiration from Planxty, The Pogues and Lankum, The Wran combines traditional and modern instrumentation, including banjo, harmonium, acoustic guitar, bass VI and drums. They are dedicated to keeping the Irish language, traditional songs and storytelling alive while continuing to push it forward in their own way. After an explosive live debut in 2025, including accoladed performances at Glastonbury, Green Man, All Together Now, and Electric Picnic, the band went on to support The Scratch and Kíla, play Dublin’s Notable NYD festival, and sell out their first Irish tour. Beginning 2026 with a sold-out UK tour, The Wran are fast establishing themselves as one of Ireland’s most vital new bands.

the-molgoggers.name: THE MOLGOGGERS
the-molgoggers.bio: The Molgoggers are an ageless gang of renegades from the South Coast of Ireland. Plundering and pillaging is part of their everyday activities and no sailing ship in Irish waters is safe from these bloodthirsty crooning pirates. They love to sing raucous sea shanties that are repetitive and easily learnt, particularly by youngsters who show no fear for these fearsome creatures. In fact, audience participation is compulsory – you have been warned! To entertain you, these mangy mongrels have sailed from their lair in Cobh, up the River Barrow and beached the Salty Dog here for the weekend. All Aboard! Arrggg!

blessed.name: BLESSED
blessed.bio: Back for their fifth year at Electric Picnic, Blessed is Ireland’s loudest two-piece band—powered by the unstoppable duo of Tony Cunningham and Jason Lynch. Known for their electrifying take on 90s dance anthems, these lads tear up the stage with nothing but two guitars, a voice that can’t be silenced and a whole lot of energy. Their signature style? High-octane, pulse-racing performances that turn nostalgic bangers into full-blown acoustic rave sessions. From Faithless to Darude, every track is a hit, reimagined with wild rhythm, relentless drive, and full crowd participation. What started as a passion project has become a festival staple—where heart meets chaos and the field goes off. If you’re looking for a set that’ll get you moving, laughing, singing, and shouting all at once, Blessed is the one to catch. No backing tracks, no filler—just two lads, two guitars, and full of madness.

these-charming-men.name: THESE CHARMING MEN
these-charming-men.bio: These Charming Men from Dublin, Ireland were formed in 1995 and to this day continue to charm fans of The Smiths and Morrissey all around the globe with their finely tuned energetic and passionate live shows. They are classed as the premier Smiths and Morrissey tribute bands or acts around at the moment. In 2025 These Charming Men sold out the 3Olympia Theatre in Dublin and continue to sell out venues around Ireland. These Charming Men have performed at the Annual Smiths/Morrissey Convention in Los Angeles since 2001 and were requested to appear in Morrissey’s absence at the Fuji Rock Festival in Japan 2004 to play to an audience of some 35,000 people. These Charming Men are always festival highlight at Electric Picnic and at many other summer festivals, These Charming Men are a must for all Smiths and Morrissey fans.

squarehead.name: SQUAREHEAD
squarehead.bio: "Fifteen years on from their seminal debut album 'Yeah Nothing', the Dublin garage rock stalwarts, Squarehead, make yet another triumphant return with their latest album 'Ossory Road'. A band that defined the late 2000's indie-DIY music scene, this new record proves that time has done nothing to dull their sharp, infectious edge. Raw, propulsive energy drives the bands live show which brilliantly bridges the gaps across their fifteen year history, moving seamlessly from the sun-drenched, surf-pop hooks of their early catalogue to the more textured layers of 'Ossory Road'. Squarehead are back, again, proving exactly why they remain one of Ireland's most fiercely cherished musical treasures" - David McEneaney - McGig Music

george-houston.name: GEORGE HOUSTON
george-houston.bio: Hailing from rural Donegal, George Houston is a genre-bending singer-songwriter praised for his poetic, cinematic sound and deeply personal themes. Since debuting in 2020, Houston has released four albums, toured with Paul Weller, and The Divine Comedy, received acclaim from BBC Radio One, RTÉ Radio One, and played Later… with Jools Holland, and The Tommy Tiernan Show. His work explores grief, queerness, and resilience, wrapped in lush harmonies and gothic-folk aesthetics.

thumper.name: THUMPER
thumper.bio: Irish alt-rockers THUMPER have released 2 highly acclaimed albums: their debut, Choice Music Prize-nominated 'Delusions of Grandeur' (2022) followed by their sophomore, 'Sleeping With The Light On' (2026). The incendiary live 6-piece have toured Ireland, the UK, and Europe extensively becoming regulars on the festival circuit appearing at the likes of Electric Picnic (IE), Other Voices (IE), Mad Cool (ESP), Reading & Leeds (UK), Iceland Airwaves (IS), Haldern Pop (DE), Rock For People (CZ), Eurosonic (NL), Reeperbahn (DE), United Artists Prague (CZ), and many more. The band has received extensive press support (Clash, Dork, The Line of Best Fit, New Noise, Punk News, Hot Press, Nialler9, Distorted Sound, Goldenplec, Louder Than War to name a few) and international airplay across BBC 6 Music, BBC Radio 1, Radio X, KEXP, Kink, Kerrang! as well as Irish stations such as RTÉ Radio 1, 2FM, Today FM, Beat102103 among others. They have also made noteworthy TV performances on RTÉ’s Tommy Tiernan Show and Other Voices and secured numerous Spotify and Apple Music editorial playlist placements and cover features.

backa-beyond.name: BACKA BEYOND
backa-beyond.bio: The Baka believe that "spirits" live in the forest who like to dance with people. Their music is designed to call these spirits to come and dance, and make peoples’ problems disappear. Festival favourites, Baka Beyond, certainly live up to this. With musicians from Cornwall, Wales, England, Congo and Sierra Leone, they mix the Spirit of the Forest with Celtic, African and modern sounds to create a positive feel-good vibe that you can’t help but move to. Let’s dance!

i-dreamed-i-dream.name: I DREAMED I DREAM
i-dreamed-i-dream.bio: I Dreamed I Dream are a four-piece from Cork, merging post-punk, dream-pop, sean-nós, and 60s girl-group influences with a sharp Corkonian edge. Their live shows blur the line between gig and theatrical exorcism - equal parts noise, catharsis, and communal tonic wine - earning Paste’s praise as “possibly the best live act in Ireland right now.” Formed in 2021 as a duo, the band quickly expanded into a four-piece, amplifying a raw, defiant sound. Their debut EP, Why Say A Lot? (2023), introduced a sardonic noise-rock-meets-shoegaze energy, while BOYOPOISONING (2025) dives deeper into chaos and self-discovery, telling a coming-of-age story about love, loss, identity, and Princess Diana. Currently in the studio recording their debut album, I Dreamed I Dream continue to push boundaries and captivate audiences across Ireland and beyond with a sound that is loud, unapologetic, unpredictable, and entirely their own.

silverbacks.name: SILVERBACKS
silverbacks.bio: Silverbacks are a band from Ireland. Their debut album, Fad (2020), instantly grabbed attention with its angular guitar work, offbeat lyrics and and infectious melodies earned praise from BBC 6 Music, NME, Stereogum, Brooklyn Vegan, and more, drawing comparisons to bands like Pavement, Parquet Courts and Television. In 2022, Silverbacks followed up with Archive Material, a record that refined their sound and solidified their place in the indie scene, garnering further acclaim. Tours across Ireland, UK, Europe and a first visit to the US followed. With their third album, Easy Being A Winner (October, 2024), Silverbacks continue to experiment with new textures and sounds while maintaining their signature playful and unpredictable style.

monsieur-pompier.name: MONSIEUR POMPIER
monsieur-pompier.bio: Monsieur Pompier’s Travelling Freakshow is a five-piece band and theatrical spectacle blending surreal cabaret with chaotic art rock. With songs about bog witches, ear fairies and inside out cats, their live shows turn into a fever dream of bizarre costumed creatures and warped storytelling. Their debut album Teatime Terrors was released on Cleopatra Records in 2021, with a second due in late 2026. After years haunting Europe’s fringe and punk scenes, they became festival favourites in Ireland. In 2025, Monsieur Pompier opened his Museum of Curiosities in Dublin, a permanent home for the wonderfully strange.

raz-and-afla.name: RAZ AND AFLA
raz-and-afla.bio: Raz Olsher & Afla Sackey: a bond that fuels a dynamic and effortless musical relationship. Their music represents a harmonious union of African influences with electronic music, full of soul, vibrant energy and captivating rhythms. The balance between Raz’s production style and Afla’s Afrocentric flavours ignited dance floors and earned the duo a glowing reputation from the very beginning. Their debut album, ‘The Cycle’, came out late 2022 and has gained critical acclaim from the likes of Gilles Peterson, Lauren Lavern, Jamz Supernova and was play listed on BBC Radio 6,1Xtra, FIP, Radio Nova as well as obtaining fans from their peers and remixing the likes of Glass Animals, Batida and Crate Classics Following their debut The Cycle, and its subsequent remix project, their sophomore LP, Echoes Of Resistance, finds the duo remaining committed to exploring new sonic territories and creating music that speaks to the universal language of rhythm and melody. Beyond their studio recordings, Raz & Afla are celebrated for their exhilarating live performances, playing shows in major festivals in France, Netherlands, Germany, Cyprus and the UK. This is a twosome expressing themselves to the world; vulnerable, truthful and exposed, it’s a personal statement that will resonate with listeners all over the world.

grooveline.name: GROOVELINE
grooveline.bio: Grooveline: Bilingual high octane sextet from the North West of Ireland described as having “the precision of Vulfpeck, the coolness of Parliament and the energy of James Brown" - HotPress Magazine. Grooveline are one of Ireland’s most dynamic and exciting upcoming bands. The 6 piece style bending band rooted in funk blend (High energy Funk, Groove, Hip-Hop, Rock , Jazz and Trad) to make a completely refreshing sound that is unlike anything in the Irish music scene. Off the back of supporting Belters Only and Jazzy as part of Virgin Media’s New series ‘The Secret Headliner’ and their recent support slots for KNEECAP, GrooveLine are fronting a new wave of the Irish language in music. With unfolding and constantly developing instrumentals, catchy melodies and raps, a rhythm section specifically designed for high energy boogying and a raw and untamed energy that brings people together to experience the freedom of truly having the craic. Grooveline’s live show is up there with the best in Ireland

shrunk-jumper.name: Shrunk Jumper
shrunk-jumper.bio: Shrunk Jumper is a two piece electronic project consisting of producers Jack Nolan and Hugh McLean. Founded in Dublin over several sessions where the duo reinterpreted “dead demos” from previous projects to blend their curated sound, drawing inspiration from hyper pop to heroin rock. The project is an amalgamation of the duos contrasting yet complimentary sonic backgrounds.

m-abh-eva.name: Méabh & Eva
m-abh-eva.bio: Eva Carroll and Méabh Mulligan are acclaimed traditional Irish musicians and singers from Dublin. Steeped in deep musical heritages, they perform as a duo—playing concertina and singing—and are prominent figures in Dublin's lively trad, folk, and singing scenes.

isp-n-agus-c-is.name: Ispíní agus Cáis
isp-n-agus-c-is.bio: Hop out of the frying pan and into a candlelight supper with Ispíní na hÉireann for Ispíní agus Cáis, as they abandon their usual set in favour of one garnished with cheese. You will hear many favourites from a time gone by, as the Ispíní break out cheesy bangers from the 1990s and 2000s

the-cobblestone-pub-s-opening-night-sess.name: The Cobblestone Pub's Opening Night Session
the-cobblestone-pub-s-opening-night-sess.bio: The iconic Cobblestone pub kicks off the whole weekend with our opening-night session — and yes, this is the one that literally broke the stage last year (true story). With the Mulligan family and friends at the helm, you already know it'll be rocking again. Come early, squeeze in, and let one of Dublin's most legendary trad institutions set the bar for everything that follows.

mahogany-gaspipes.name: Mahogany Gaspipes
mahogany-gaspipes.bio: Together for almost 12 years — and nameless for most of them — the Mahogany Gaspipes are Derek Copley, Alan "the Greek" Mac and Dylan Darcy at the core, rarely on stage alone. They're forever joined by a rotating cast of some of Ireland's most talented musicians— the likes of Síle Ryan, Carlito, Camile Champernaud and Brian Duggan — so don't be surprised to find ten of them crammed onto a tiny stage, blasting out tunes with gusto. A rousing bunch of Irish trad musicians and like-minded souls, they deal in wild, explosive, raw-energy traditional music. Hold onto your caps for the rapid reels, the bejaysus jigs and the diddily damhsaí — plus a few surging songs to stomp your boots to. A wild, feral show, not to be missed.

the-len-collective.name: The Len Collective
the-len-collective.bio: The Len Collective are a group of traditional Irish musicians from Dublin. Though only officially forming the Collective in 2022, these group of friends have been playing and attending festivals together since they were children. Go into the Cobblestone at any hour of the day or night and there's a good chance you'll find at least one of them hanging about. Since forming in 2022, the Len Collective have performed at multiple festivals including the Otherside, All Together Now, Féile na Gealaí, Féile Nasc, Lá Mór na Gaeilge, Smithfield Fleadh, Me Auld Flower, Electric Picnic, St Patrick’s day festival Dublin, Music in the Courtyard @ IMMA, the Tradition Now series at the National Concert Hall. The Len collective have represented Ireland abroad at the Tonn Nua festival in Berlin, Embassy of Ireland Warsaw visit for St Brigid’s Day, Yn Chuinnaght Celtic Gathering at the Isle of Man and the residency at the Irish Pavilion Expo in Osaka, Japan.

the-lines.name: The Lines
the-lines.bio: The Lines are a four-piece original Irish folk band from Dublin, formed in 2024, The group features singer-guitarists Karl O'Connell and Aron Fox, Rían Doyle on bass and Rob Collins on tin whistle. They're regularly joined by banjo and mandolin player Paahto Cummins (Ispini na hÉireann), adding a vibrant edge to their live sound. Rooted in the tradition of classic ballad groups like The Dubliners and The Wolfe Tones, The Lines also bring a modern twist-infusing their music with the raw energy of punk and indie rock influences, echoing the likes of The Pogues. Since their formation, they've built a reputation for raucous, high-energy live shows, selling out venues including Little Whelan's, Sin E O’Neills bar in Derry, all while holding a monthly residency in Mother Reillys in Rathmines. They have also travelled abroad to Glasgow to the famous Vicar Street Social at McChuills bar. The band is currently working on new songs which will be released summer 2026

ciaran-moran.name: Ciaran Moran
ciaran-moran.bio: Ciarán Moran is a Dublin‑based singer‑songwriter whose music blends folk, indie and rock with raw, socially conscious storytelling. Drawing heavily from his North Inner City roots, Moran writes honest, emotionally charged songs that connect deeply with audiences through lived experience, strong melodies and a powerful vocal delivery.

the-labourers.name: The Labourers
the-labourers.bio: The Labourers are a band driven by Irish Trad, Indie Rock and energy. 2025 was a mark of success for the band, releasing hits like ‘Bittersweet’ and ‘Too Fast’. The 2026 release of ‘One Long Goodbye’, shows a new progression for the band; a little taste of what’s to come.

special-guest.name: Special Guest
special-guest.bio: One of the hottest young bands in the country right now — and we predict that's about to go stratospheric. They've already built a serious following, and it's only a matter of time before everyone knows their name. Catch them on Spike Island while you still can up this close — miss this one and you'll be kicking yourself.

dudley-s-bar-lounge-session-on-tour.name: Dudley's Bar & Lounge Session on Tour
dudley-s-bar-lounge-session-on-tour.bio: The legendary Sunday-night session from Dudley's Bar & Lounge in the heart of the Liberties hits the road for Electric Picnic — bringing Dublin's finest trad straight to Spike Island for late night Friday tunes. Same wild energy, same packed-pub buzz, out under the festival sky.

al-baker.name: Al Baker
al-baker.bio: Al Baker is a Dublin-born singer-songwriter whose eclectic musical journey spans the raw energy of rock bands and the innovative pulse of electronic music to the soulful embrace of traditional folk. Twice steeped in academic music studies, Al has honed his craft into a unique sound characterized by acoustic textures and an upbeat country twist. His songs weave abstract imagery with themes of insomnia, life's relentless pressures, and heartbreak, creating a captivating and deeply resonant musical narrative. 1st release in June 2026.

kettleboilers.name: Kettleboilers
kettleboilers.bio: Kettle Boilers are a high-energy, Trad-influenced folk rock band hailing from Galway. Their debut album ‘The Fear’ was self-released on August 23rd 2024. The Boilers craft their own unique blend of music, taking broad inspiration from acts such as Horslips and Lankum to rock and grunge bands from the 90's. Their live act is highly acclaimed as an upbeat rock and trad experience with audience members ranging from céilí dancing to bopping around a mosh pit. The gang are currently writing their second independent album, expanding on their sound, exploring ceol as Ghaeilge, and honing their craft. They are very excited to be back gigging around Ireland summer 2026

kk-lewis.name: KK Lewis
kk-lewis.bio: KK Lewis is the Dublin artist you need on your festival radar right now. Blending soul, R&B and cinematic pop, her music hits that rare sweet spot.. intimate enough to stop you in your tracks, big enough to fill a field. Her breakout single Pigeon Man took on a life of its own online, racking up over 3 million views and 26k+ user-generated videos, while follow-up One Step Behind, RTE Radio 1's Track of the Week earned her comparisons to the best of classic soul. Live with her four-piece band, KK brings a neo soul and R&B-influenced show - equal parts craic and gut-punch, the kind of set you walk away from still thinking about. Backed by a tight, jazz-leaning ensemble, she moves with a confidence reminiscent of Olivia Dean and RAYE, while still retaining her own distinctive flair. She's currently recording her debut project with producer Joseph Rodgers (beabadoobee, Rina Sawayama) and this might be your last chance to catch her on a small stage before everything changes.

trad-folkin-raps.name: Trad Folkin Raps
trad-folkin-raps.bio: Trad Folkin Raps is a collective of Limerick artists that bring you a heady mix of trad and rap.

the-spudguns.name: The Spudguns
the-spudguns.bio: The Spudguns are a band from Ireland founded by four friends. Bringing you rock n’roll from the Garden County. Working out of their studio “Big Beef Sound” in Arklow Co. Wicklow, the band has refined their DIY-style approach to recording, while shaping their unique sound. Their music takes inspiration from surf rock and garage rock, with subtle touches of psychedelia. They have played up and down Ireland in venues such as Whelans, Sin É, Fred Zeppelins, The Harbour Bar, and at Electric Picnic 2025. 2026 consisted of an Irish tour in counties in different corners of the country. The band’s music has received praise from outlets such as ‘RTE’, ‘Hot Press’ and ‘Void Magazine’. Their debut EP ‘Notions’ was released in December 2025.

burnchurch.name: Burnchurch
burnchurch.bio: Burnchurch is a young folk-pop band from Kilkenny, Ireland, made up of talented siblings who blend Irish roots with a modern sound. Known for their high-energy live shows and feel-good atmosphere, the band is making a name for itself through a growing catalogue of original songs that combine catchy melodies, strong storytelling, and contemporary folk, jazz and traditional influences. From busking on Kilkenny’s Parade to performing on bigger stages, Burnchurch continues to build momentum with music that is fresh, authentic, and unmistakably their own.

isp-n-na-h-ireann.name: Ispíní na hÉireann
isp-n-na-h-ireann.bio: Ispíní na hÉireann are a feral Folk-Alternative Irish music collective from Dublin, Ireland. They formed in 2018 and are fronted by Tomás Mulligan, Paahto Cummins, and Declan Gillen. Steeped in Dublin's rich traditional music scene, the band brings together some of Ireland's most exciting and talented contemporary musicians, cultivating a sound that is fiercely original and unmistakably Irish. Their music blends virtuosic original compositions with bold re-imaginings of classic tunes, fusing technical mastery with sharp wit, storytelling, and social commentary — creating performances that are as thought-provoking as they are electrifying. Following the success of their debut album The Hard Working Men, the band released their critically acclaimed second record Poxtail Soup, showcasing their trademark mix of energy, irreverence, and heart. With a growing audience across Ireland, the UK, and Europe, and a reputation for exhilarating live shows, Ispíní na hÉireann continue to redefine what contemporary Irish music can be.

the-fada-live-session.name: The Fada Live Session
the-fada-live-session.bio: Spike Island hands Saturday night to FADA for a session of their own. The up-and-coming four-piece FADA brings an electrifying blend of folk, traditional Irish music and classic ballads — high-energy trad and crowd-wide sing-alongs honed in Dublin pubs like the James Connolly and John's Bar. Rian Breathnach on vocals and guitar, Ríona Howlin on fiddle, Luke McCann on concertina and Cathal Murphy on cajon and vocals. Expect reels at full tilt and a stage that won't stay still.

darkey-kelly-s-session.name: Darkey Kelly's Session
darkey-kelly-s-session.bio: The ultra long-running, mega Darkey Kelly's pub session — a Sunday-afternoon institution in Dublin — takes over the "morning" of the Spike Island stage with several hours of rolling traditional music. This one's open: bring your instrument, pull up a chair, and play a tune alongside some of Dublin's best-known trad musicians or just enjoy the magic. All welcome — the perfect easy start before the night takes off.

saltaire.name: Saltaire
saltaire.bio: Saltaire brings together three distinct musical voices shaped by years performing in acclaimed Irish traditional and folk bands, alongside extensive session work. The trio—singer/cellist Kaitlin Cullen-Verhauz, guitarist Ian Kinsella, and bodhrán/bouzouki player Conor Lyons—create a bold, dynamic sound that blends haunting textures, rich storytelling, original songs, reimagined folk ballads, and traditional tunes. Their music is both fresh and timeless, driven by the interplay of cello, guitar, bouzouki, and bodhrán. In February 2026, Saltaire released their debut EP Only Moonlight to widespread critical acclaim, receiving praise from Hot Press, RTÉ Radio 1, BBC Ulster, Irish Music Magazine, Hidden Track, NuMuze, and others. The band was selected as an official showcase act at both Your Roots Are Showing in Belfast and the Culture Ireland TradFest showcase in Dublin. International invitations quickly followed, including performances in Australia, France, Spain, and upcoming festival appearances in North America. In March, renowned producer Josh Rogosin (NPR Tiny Desk) invited the band to perform and record for his Global Sound Concert series at Windmill Lane Recording Studios. Self-described as “a band of backers,” Saltaire’s music is rooted in collaboration, drawing on close creative relationships with many of Ireland’s leading folk and traditional musicians.

n-in-n.name: Nóiníní
n-in-n.bio: Nóiníní are a 6 piece, all-female (plus Derek) traditional Irish music outfit, based in Co Kildare. Since first forming in their early teens, Noiníní has honed a specific sound and stage craft over the past 20-plus years, their natural friendship creating and effortless sense of fun at their live shows, while also intuitively bringing to their performance equal measures of sensitive, captivating and invigorating tunes and songs which have found favour at their many live shows around the country over their career, most recently performing at the inaugural Feile Liam O Flynn. Members of the band are: Ais Keogh (fiddle, Sinead Keogh (guitar, vocals, concertina), Mary Ann Ryan (uileann pipes, flute) and Maeve O'Hara (percussion, flute).Sara Bradshaw (mandolin) Derek Copley(bazouki)

laura-jo.name: Laura Jo
laura-jo.bio: Laura Jo is a North Longford singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist whose music blends Irish traditional roots with contemporary folk, jazz and Americana. Her single “Bright Eyes” won the Hot Press & IBI A New Local Hero Wildcard Award. A seasoned live performer, she has toured internationally and appeared on major festival stages including Doolin Folk Fest, Electric Picnic, ATN, Forest Fest, Galway Folk Fest and Galway International Arts Festival, alongside national broadcast performances on RTÉ’s The Late Late Show, RTÉ Radio 1’s Ray D’Arcy Show and TG4’s Geantraí.

caoimh-n.name: Caoimhín
caoimh-n.bio: CAOIMHÍN is a producer, singer, and multi-instrumentalist re-imagining old Ireland in a new age. His psychedelic beat-driven music combines traditional dance tunes, an Gaeilge and native Irish folk songs with elements such as sampling, gated vocal loops and ambient synth soundscapes, paying homage to the long lineage of indigenous Gaelic music on which he was reared while simultaneously breaking new ground at its frontiers.

friends-of-the-relics.name: Friends of the Relics
friends-of-the-relics.bio: Come come beautiful Eileen, come for a ride with me To see the Friends of the Relics In all their finery! They'll get you up and they won't let you down! With more styles than a hairdresser’s handbag, a night with the Relics will linger long in the temporal lobe. Punk, funk, folk, reggae and more…the Friends of the Relics have it all at the altar of craic. The Relics are..Shay Nolan on vocals, Dylan Darcy on guitar, Derek Copley on banjo, Aminah Dastan on vocals, Camille Champernaud on bass and Griffo on the drums.

megatrad.name: Megatrad
megatrad.bio: With a sound best described as an exalted manifestation of Irish Trad, megaTRAD meld their cultural musical heritage with diverse individual musical experiences, bolstered by the contemporary nuances of stomp, bass, and pedal FX boards. The outcome is an innovative and exhilarating auditory journey, affectionately termed "Tradscendental" by their enthusiastic fanbase. With an improvisatory approach to their performances every megaTRAD show will be completely unique and never to be heard in that particular arrangement again, guaranteeing each audience authenticity and a once in a lifetime auditory experience. megaTRAD have also just released their debut album "It begins with a..." and invite you to join them on musical journey where tradition meets innovation, and where every note is an adventure! Get ready to be immersed in the contemporary, rich, and lively sounds of 21st Century Irish traditional music - megaTRAD style!

jordo-byrne.name: Jordo Byrne
jordo-byrne.bio:
From the very first beat, Jordo Byrne turns the dancefloor into a celebration. Blending infectious house grooves, disco sparkle, funk-fuelled rhythms, and alternative influences, his sets are built to keep crowds moving and smiling long after the music stops.

Known for seamless mixing, unexpected selections, and an instinct for reading the room, Jordo creates a journey that balances timeless classics with fresh underground sounds. Whether it’s a sun-soaked festival stage, a packed club, or an intimate late-night session, he delivers high-energy performances packed with feel-good vibes and irresistible grooves.

Expect funky basslines, uplifting house rhythms, disco-infused euphoria, and genre-bending moments that bring people together on the dancefloor. 

If you’re looking for a set that feels fresh, authentic, and impossible to stand still to, Jordo Byrne is a name you won’t forget.

House. Disco. Funk. Alternative. One mission: keep the crowd dancing.

floody.name: FLOODY
floody.bio:
Floody is an emerging DJ from Dublin, Ireland who plays everything between Hardtrance, Bounce,Hardhouse and techno. 

Floody has played in clubs and all over Ireland aswell as clubs overseas in Ibiza and Portugal supporting some of the biggest artists in the Industry.

His productions have been supported by the likes of Hannah Laing, Patrick Mason, Cloudy, Lee Ann Robert’s and Tanja Minju and he likes to bring most of his own tracks into his live sets.

Catch him play at our Artlot stage on the Thursday this year for a high energy set.

the-wires.name: The Wires
the-wires.bio:
The Wires are a 3-piece hard rock band hailing from the depths of southeast Ireland, in Wexford. The whole aim of this 3-piece power group is to bring a new, unique sound and presence back to the music scene, with each member having varying influences, each of them bring a wild element of sound and throw it in one loud, energetic, and obnoxious mixing pot.

With echoing determination, The Wires are slowly but surely climbing the ladder, with their most recent release of debut EP Frogspawn, they have big plans bubbling against the underbelly of Ireland.

the-voodoo-kitchen.name: The Voodoo Kitchen
the-voodoo-kitchen.bio:
The Voodoo Kitchen are a rock trio with Brazilian roots, founded in 2016 by bassist, vocalist and songwriter Rod Rosica.  Based in Dublin for over seven years, the band have built a strong reputation on the Irish live circuit, earning praise for their powerful performances and hard rock sound with a blues-driven edge.

The current lineup features Rod Rosica (bass/vocals), Igor Tavares (guitar) and Billy Katsikas (drums), combining tight musicianship with raw, dynamic energy on stage.

The Voodoo Kitchen have released a series of singles and EPs that showcase their evolving sound and distinctive musical identity. Their latest release, Dancing With Angels & Demons, was accompanied by the music video for the track Look Away (Again) and further highlights the band's powerful songwriting and unmistakable rock 'n' roll spirit.

lemonade-shoelace.name: Lemonade Shoelace
lemonade-shoelace.bio:
Inspired by the surreal and grounded in modern pop, Lemonade Shoelace had created a bedrock of psychedelic sounds, weaving them into a nostalgic yet futuristic journey of honesty, reflection and playfulness. He has journeyed as far as Mexico City, Texas, Paris and Sweden performing his psychedelic haze of indie music, and his ear for a catchy melody alongside his vivid auditory imagination has created a world of vibrant colours and rhythms on par with the likes of Tame Impala. 


Having supported the likes of Yungblud, Unknown Mortal Orchestra & Sports Team, Lemonade Shoelace has taken a break from touring in recent years to focus rigorously on songwriting and experimenting in the studio, emerging with Magnetised: a collection of prismatic five psych-pop songs proving a sharper focus, brighter palettes and a new era for sound and aesthetics.

mac-steady.name: Mac Steady
mac-steady.bio: Mac Steady are a five-piece sound experience hailing from Dublin + Kilkenny. Heavily influenced by sounds from jazz, soul, indie and alternative rock, they’ve carved out a name for themselves on the Irish music scene. Since emerging in 2024, they’ve become a regular presence on the Dublin gig circuit, earning attention for their dynamic live performances and distinctive sound. Definitely a must see over the Electric Picnic weekend.

smithereens.name: Smithereens
smithereens.bio: Formed in Cork, Ireland in 2024, Smithereens are a five piece Jazz/Rock band who have been making their mark on the Irish music scene and abroad. Their debut album Emergency Entrance (2024) immediately made an impact on fans in Ireland, and they have since performed sold out shows nationwide. Examples include Live at St. Luke’s (2025) ,The Kino (2024,2025), and also Next door records (2026) in London. [They have played in numerous music festivals such as Féile Solas, Forbidden Fruit, Guinness Cork Jazz Festival and Clonakilty International Guitar Festival. They’ve gained the attention of magazines such as Banjaxed media and NuMuze. Fans enjoy their fusion of sophisticated jazz harmony with the angular, distorted guitar lines and raucous vocals of grunge.

cro-the.name: Croíthe
cro-the.bio: Croíthe (KREE-HA) are a Dublin-based post-punk/shoegaze band making waves with their dark, emotive sound. Their debut EP, A Brief Respite, hit #1 on Ireland’s Best-Selling Charts and #11 on the Independent Charts, earning praise from BBC Radio 6’s Steve Lamacq. After a busy 2025 touring the UK and Europe, 2026 promises to be a big year, with headline shows and further touring cementing their status as one of Dublin’s most exciting new acts.

kay.name: KAY
kay.bio: KAY is an Irish roller skater and dancer whose work spans festivals, live music, and stage productions across Ireland and the UK. Credits include CMAT’s No More Virgos, Hellfest, and numerous large-scale live performances. Returning to Electric Picnic for her third year, she combines powerful skating, dance, and performance artistry to create unforgettable moments on stage.

claudia-o.name: Claudia O
claudia-o.bio:
A devotee of dance music, Claudia came of age in Dublin at the dawn of the rave scene in 1991. What started as a passion for the culture grew into decades of dedicated vinyl collecting and deep musical exploration.

After travelling the world as cabin crew and experiencing some of the best clubs on the planet, she took time to raise a family—always immersed in music, always digging—before stepping into DJ’ing with intention and purpose.

In 2020, Claudia launched a boutique festival rooted in community, connection, and cutting-edge sound. Now seven years strong, it continues to showcase some of Ireland’s finest DJs.

Stepping behind the decks in 2024, she now channels years of musical obsession into dynamic sets. This is dance music driven by passion, history, and a love for bringing people together on the floor.

You can tune in to Claudia's show every Thursday from 5-6pm on @playfmdublin

adzyob.name: AdzyOB
adzyob.bio:
Making his return to the Artlot stage, AdzyOB is a rising multi-genre DJ who has performed at some of Dublin’s leading venues, including The Sound House, Twenty Two, and Wigwam.

As a member of the rapidly growing InsideOut collective, he has been helping to cement the group’s reputation as one of the exciting new forces in the Irish rave scene.

Expect an energetic blend of hard bounce, UK garage, and hard dance, delivered with high energy and a crowd-focused approach that keeps the dancefloor moving from start to finish.

mode.name: Modeā
mode.bio:
Modea is widely considered one of the most compelling voices in the new wave of electronic music. The Irish artist has carved out a distinct sonic identity, merging raw energy with powerful, euphoric records designed to move both the body and the mind. Rapidly building global momentum, he is emerging as one of Ireland's most exciting electronic exports. Born and raised in Donegal, Modeã's musical journey began at just seven years old, inspired by his parents' love of electronic music.
From those early beginnings, he developed a deep understanding of emotion in sound, something that now defines his work. Whether in the studio or performing on stage, his focus remains the same: creating moments that feel uplifting, expansive, and unforgettable.

the-dirty-circus.name: The Dirty Circus
the-dirty-circus.bio: The Dirty Circus is a high-energy burlesque and cabaret experience featuring an electrifying mix of Burlesque, Drag, Circus, Divas, and Pole performances. Expect dazzling costumes, jaw-dropping talent, bold personalities, and unforgettable entertainment as world-class artists take the stage with glamour, comedy, and plenty of attitude. Sexy, spectacular, and delightfully outrageous, The Dirty Circus delivers a thrilling night of variety entertainment that celebrates confidence,diversity,  creativity, and pure show-stopping fun

the-gladstone-band.name: The Gladstone Band
the-gladstone-band.bio: The Gladstone Band is a trad and folk trio formed in 2024 in Dublin, and is made up of brothers Adam and Patrick Hutton, Tim Sheridan, and Jamie Kealy. Their stripped-back, high-energy sound harkens back to that of the early Dubliners, while their layered harmonies recall musicians such as Stan Rogers. They play a mix of traditional and folk standards, alongside their own original repertoire.

and-he-the-fool.name: and he, the fool
and-he-the-fool.bio:
AND HE, THE FOOL are the new Dublin septet. Seamlessly blending their combined tastes for the theatricality of Art Rock and Psychedelic Pop, they tint their sound with the ethereal harmony and sentiment of Melancholia at their saddest and of Contemporary Soul and their most celebratory. With all of this emotion moving to a New Wave informed groove, the fools have already established an ever evolving, diverse yet distinctive voice.
‘Their live sets have gathered a lot of buzz already; showcasing hot-swapping lead vocals, tight rhythmic musicianship and mellifluous layers of harmony carrying the show from moody pensive tension to bursts of agony and euphoria.
 
 Early attendees have been drawing comparisons to acts ranging from Jeff Buckley to Talking Heads, Hayley Williams to Black Country, New Road.

curfew.name: Curfew
curfew.bio: North Dublin-based original Alternative-Hard Rock music makers. Our debut album 'Black Doll's Eyes' is out now.

ember.name: Ember
ember.bio: Ember are a Dublin-based alternative rock band writing songs about longing, nostalgia and the things we can’t quite let go of. Their sound drifts between the dreamy and the heavy, combining haunting melodies, honest songwriting and powerful guitar-driven arrangements. Whether quiet and intimate or loud and cathartic, Ember’s music is driven by feeling first.

the-wu.name: The WU
the-wu.bio:
The WU are an alternative three piece band from Raheny, North Dublin, consisting of childhood friends Daniel Brady, Ciaran White and Daniel Kearns. The band seeks to blend 60s influences with their own brand of indie.

Formed while friends at school, the band has relentlessly gigged around the country, honing their craft on the circuit.

Earlier in 2026, The WU were named in Hot Press as “Hot for 2026” due to their notoriously energetic shows and catchy hooks. In the past year, the band have filled some of Ireland’s most iconic venues including The Roisin Dubh, Dolan’s and Whelan’s and have performed explosive festival sets at Electric Picnic and Ireland Music Week 2025.

Since the release of acclaimed singles, “The Weight” and “Off My Head”, the three Dubliners have started to make their mark on the Irish alternative scene, making sure they don’t take life too seriously along the way.

seanem.name: SEANEM
seanem.bio:
SEANEM is a 12-year-old DJ and emerging producer from Dublin, whose passion for electronic music began behind a pair of Technics SL-1210s, learning on vinyl and mixing purely by ear from an early age. Having grown up immersed in dance music and spending time in Ibiza every year of his life, he draws inspiration from trance, progressive and Balearic house, bringing a unique energy and maturity to his sets.

Since making his public debut at just 10 years old, SEANEM has performed at festivals across Ireland and internationally at Amsterdam Dance Event (ADE), as well as venues across Ibiza, Mexico, Belgium and Germany. In 2026, he secured his first Ibiza residency, another milestone in a rapidly growing career.

barry-bolger.name: Barry Bolger
barry-bolger.bio:
Hailing from The Royal County Barry Bolger started Djing over 25 years ago and was co founder and resident Dj for Liquid Promotions which ran events in Puddenhill, playing alongside Dublin legends the Banana boys and Temple Theatre resident Darren Flynn as well as a host of local Djs from the North East.

After recently returning to the scene Barry has secured gigs in Holland for Luminosity Beach Festival after parties for the last 2 years

He has supported Mauro Piccotto for North East Old Skool as part of there 8th year anniversary celebrations.

Delivering energetic and lively sets and with a passion for Trance, Tech Trance, Techno and Classics he is sure to get a dance floor moving.

a-k.name: A/K
a-k.bio:
A/K returns to the Artlot stage for his second appearance, bringing the energy and sound that have become his trademark. Moving effortlessly through the many shades of house music, from deep and groovy rollers to uplifting peak-time moments, his sets are all about creating a connection with the crowd and keeping the dancefloor moving.

With a residency in Mallorca and appearances at some of Dublin’s best-known venues, including 3Olympia, A/K has built a reputation for delivering memorable sets packed with rhythm, atmosphere, and plenty of feel-good moments. His sound is driven by infectious grooves, rolling basslines, and carefully selected tracks that build naturally and keep the energy flowing.

Whether it’s a sun-soaked daytime session or a late-night dancefloor, A/K brings a genuine passion for house music and a knack for reading the crowd, making every set feel like its own unique journey.

sharpson.name: Sharpson
sharpson.bio: Hailing from Dublin and now based in London, the multi-genre producer and "Backwards DJ" Sharpson has spent 16 years causing chaos in the Irish electronic music scene. Renowned for his high-octane performances, he’s as likely to crowd-surf or MC as he is to mix with the decks completely upside down or backwards.  His infamous, chaotic raves at Electric Picnic’s ‘Granny’s Gaff’ have become an unmissable staple on every festival-goer’s bucket list. Blending nostalgic 90s rave culture, breakbeats, and pounding techno, his sets are a masterclass in dance-floor destruction. Expect a heavy dose of Dublin mannerisms integrated into UK rave tracks, alongside unexpected nods to old-school anthems like Scooter, DJ Cammy, and Basshunter. Sharpson is a pure, energetic mad lad. Catch him closing the Artlot Mainstage on Saturday.

phil-kenny.name: Phil Kenny
phil-kenny.bio: Philip is  a freelance autistic advocate who has done talks in a variety of educational,civil as well as medical institutions on the lived experiences of autism. He recently released his latest video work 'Myriad' with support from culture date with dublin8 festival  which furthers his explorations of autism and difference through spoken word. He recently shared an event with Author  Colin Barrett in a discussion of both of their works as a part of the Maynooth University Arts and Minds Festival.

the-vagabond-queen.name: THE VAGABOND QUEEN
the-vagabond-queen.bio:
Dragging spoken word straight out of its skin, The Vagabond Queen is the sonic embodiment of a one woman revolt - collapsing her performance art into a seductive assault to the senses. An unpredictable ritual rooted in the presence of transformation.

Her immersive expression is a living force: brutal in its beauty, unflinching, intimate and shaped by the raw truth of lived experience that refuses to remain silent.

An Irish and international performer described as magnetic, powerful and hypnotic, she is a devastatingly honest voice that speaks from grit and bone. This is spoken word from another world. Unbound. Alive in a fever dream.

mykology.name: Mykology
mykology.bio:
Mykology are a Dublin-based indie folk trio made up of songwriter Mick O’Gorman alongside Christina “Crispy” Quill on banjo/slide guitar and Evan Heird on double bass. Their live shows centre around close harmonies, acoustic songwriting and atmospheric arrangements blending folk, americana and indie influences.

Following support from national radio and a growing run of festival and live appearances around Ireland, the band are currently releasing new material throughout 2026

some-one-s-sons.name: Some One's Sons
some-one-s-sons.bio:
Some One’s Sons are one of Ireland’s most exciting emerging folk acts, blending traditions of Irish folk music with contemporary songwriting and raw storytelling. The five-piece from Mullingar have earned a reputation as one of Ireland’s most dynamic live folk acts, delivering powerful performances and original songs that capture the realities, struggles, humour, and spirit of modern Irish life.

Drawing inspiration from The Clancy Brothers, Planxty and Christy Moore, the Sons have built a reputation for original songs that blend heartfelt storytelling with the energy and spirit of modern Irish folk music. In 2026, they released their debut EP The Boom Is Back, featuring fan favourites including The Chance to Feel Alive, Paddy O and the title track The Boom is Back.

kapayja.name: Kapayja
kapayja.bio: Kapayja are a four-piece alternative rock band from Dublin, Ireland, crafting a sound equal parts cinematic, grungy, and haunting. Rooted in a shared instinct to serve the song above all else, they draw from a wide palette of influences to create something raw and immersive, balancing polished musicianship with a gritty edge. Since emerging, they have built momentum across 2025/26, earning support from Hot Press, BBC Introducing, Radio X, and RTE 2FM. Their debut EP gained strong radio backing and praise, while a sold-out headline show at Whelan's (Dublin, Ireland) and appearance at The Great Escape 2026 (Brighton, UK) cements their reputation as a powerful live act.

child-of-prague.name: Child of Prague
child-of-prague.bio:
Child of Prague is a band formed in 2022 born out of the alternative rock scene in Dublin.
Composed of six multi-instrumentalists, Jack McDonnell (guitar, vocals), Adam Tracey (guitar,
vocals), Rachel Baum (saxophone, violin, vocals), Amelia Durac (violin, guitar, vocals), Miranda
Gallacher (drums), and Noah Edwards (bass), the band is known for its genre-defying sound.
Each member comes from a different musical background which seamlessly blends jazz,
classical and Irish traditional music influences into their folk-rock sound. Their debut EP ‘Clothed
in the Sun’, was met to critical acclaim and they have been pulling live audiences across
Ireland, the UK and Europe. They are set to play at the widely renowned music festival Left of
the Dial in Rotterdam this October, and are supporting Irish punk band Gurriers for their Dublin
headline show at the Olympia Theatre in November.

the-blow-in-s.name: The Blow In's
the-blow-in-s.bio: The Blow In’s are an Irish folk/rock band hailing from County Kerry consisting of Cian O’Leary, Oisin O’Regan and Darragh Brosnan. The Blow In’s are known for their energetic and engaging live performances. They pride themselves in spreading their music world-wide. The Blow In’s unique sound makes their shows so memorable, catching the attention of artists such as The Mary Wallopers, James Vincent McMarrow, Ispini na hEireann and Aslan. Influenced by bands such as The Pogues, Oasis & The Waterboys, The Blow In’s have a unique desire to put their own mark on the Irish music scene. The Blow In’s SOLD OUT their Debut Headline show in Mike The Pies in April 2026 and plan to perform more shows across the country this year.

budly.name: BUDLY
budly.bio:
Based in Dublin, BUDLY curates high-energy sets shaped by hard house, groovy techno, and fast-paced underground club sounds. He has become a growing presence within the Irish scene through appearances in mainly Dublin and Waterford while also working to build community-focused events with his collective Essemble. 

An established support act, BUDLY has shared the stage with legends including KIRK, MERÖ, NANCYLIVE, MASSMEDIUM/CLUBCAVIAR, OXER, KAYCEE, FLOODY, FENSKA & many more.

Following performances at Electric Picnic in both 2024 and 2025, he continues to push his sound further with a style centred around bounce and late-night rave energy. Having recently expanded his reach into the UK with an appearance at Gemfest 2026 in June, BUDLY returns to the ARTLOT stage ready to deliver another massive set! Catch him Sunday from 9pm-10pm!

dj-beks.name: DJ BEKS
dj-beks.bio:
DJ BEKS aka Bekah Molony is a Dublin sound selector, presenter and cultural producer known for bringing infectious energy and eclectic taste to every dancefloor. Her sets blend house, latin, UKG, electro and bass-driven sounds into vibrant journeys designed to keep people moving. Expect global influences, unexpected edits, feel good dance music and plenty of moments that will have you hugging the person next to you by the time you're screaming ONE MORE TUNE.

Since making her debut in 2025, DJ BEKS has quickly built momentum with appearances at Electric Picnic, Fuinneamh, All Together Now, Beyond the Pale and Cork Jazz Weekend, alongside sets at some of Dublin’s favourite venues including Pawnshop, Hang Dai, Hen’s Teeth and Fidelity. With a growing reputation for joyful and unexpected selections, she’s fast becoming one of Ireland’s most exciting new DJs to watch.

rathaus.name: RATHAUS
rathaus.bio:
Your favourite queer party returns to Electric Picnic’s ArtLot for another very sexy takeover.

RATHAUS is a Dublin-based collective known for its high-energy blend of electronic music, performance art and radical queer expression. Built around community, connection and self-expression, Rathaus has become a staple of Ireland’s underground queer scene through its hedonistic club nights and immersive festival takeovers.

Dedicated to championing underrepresented queer talent, the collective creates spaces where people can come together, celebrate and be unapologetically themselves.

Soundtracking this year’s takeover are RATHAUS favourites Charlois and Máthair, serving up a mix of sexy techno, latintek and trance, alongside the collective’s resident dancers.

Expect big energy, beautiful chaos and plenty of reasons to stay longer than planned.

stevie-mcd.name: Stevie McD
stevie-mcd.bio: Stevie Mac is a dancefloor devotee and festival fanatic making his Electric Picnic debut this year. Expect feel-good disco infused with old-school flair and funky house grooves that keep the energy high and the crowd moving. His sets are vibrant, nostalgic, and crafted for serious good vibes

jack-madden.name: Jack Madden
jack-madden.bio: Dublin has had many emerging artists on the scene but nobody quite like this. Jack Madden is a Dublin-based DJ, producer, and musician making his Electric Picnic debut with Seomra Boil in 2026. Known for delivering high energy sets packed with house tunes and hard groove rhythms, it’s guaranteed to be an unforgettable set. Having played clubs and events across Ireland and internationally this year, it’s time to take the party to the forest. Whether warming up a room or pushing peak time energy, his sound is rooted in old school influences and dance floor classics, along with some originals. With a fast-growing presence on the Irish electronic music scene, Jack Madden is bringing his signature blend of groove and energy to Electric Picnic 2026

paulo.name: Paulo
paulo.bio: Half Portuguese, Half Irish,100% Passion Paulo infuses the soulful rhythms of disco with the pulsing heartbeat of house, all through a nostalgic lens shaped by the VHS flicker of the 80s creating the soundtrack to your night. The Organiser of The Discobox Truck & Collective he is bringing the glitter and sparkle of disco to towns across Ireland.

dj-aaron-lynam.name: DJ Aaron Lynam
dj-aaron-lynam.bio: With 18 years behind the decks, Aaron has carved his place as one of Navan’s most dynamic DJs. Supporting acts such as Jenny Green, Lisa Lashes,Jeremy Olander & Fehrplay, Paul van Dyk, Giuseppe Ottaviani, Paul Webster and Judge Jules to name a few As a key member of the Discobox Collective,He’s earned a reputation as the collective’s “right‑hand man,” who never fails to bring the noise.

bl-thnaid.name: BLÁTHNAID
bl-thnaid.bio: A Kerry DJ/Producer based in Dublin she’s been electrifying Irish dancefloors with her euphoric, high-energy sets. Known for blending progressive house, hard house, speed garage, and progressive trance, she has enjoyed a rapid rise since her standout set at Tengu as a finalist for the Cupra ‘On the Pulse’ x Four Four Magazine Beyond the Pale DJ competition 2025. Since then, she has played in Ibiza, Tenerife, and Malta. Beyond the DJ booth, she is actively shaping a more inclusive electronic music scene. Stepping into the world of event promotion, she recently launched ‘DÚIL’, a dedicated club night focused on spotlighting local, underrepresented, and FLINTA DJs. BLÁTHNAID is not to be missed!

luke-grogan.name: Luke Grogan
luke-grogan.bio: Luke Grogan is a Dublin-based DJ known for his sharp mixing, high-energy performances, and crowd-focused sets. Inspired by the iconic sounds of 90s dance music, he blends uplifting trance, driving hard house, and timeless house grooves to create unforgettable dancefloor moments. With a passion for rhythm, atmosphere, and technical precision, Luke delivers powerful sets packed with energy, nostalgia, and modern flair, making him one of Dublin’s exciting rising talents on the electronic music scene.

leon-carter.name: Leon Carter
leon-carter.bio: From Coolock, Dublin. Who’s passion for music took him down the path of becoming a Dj blending multiple genres and bouncing off the crowd’s atmosphere understanding the vibe, and playing the right track at the right time!!!
