Choose your palette, pattern and intensity, and we’ll craft a one-of-a-kind piece that celebrates individuality and self-expression. Made from durable cotton-poly blends using eco-conscious materials, every design is infused with love, energy and a little bit of magic. Join the new tie-dye revolution and wear your creativity proudly.

shiv-hickey.name: Shiv Hickey
shiv-hickey.bio: Shiv Hickey is a writer, actor, and Artistic Director of After Midnight Theatre. She firmly believes playing pretend is one of the best things you can do - no matter how old you are! Through games, stories, and a whole lot of "what if," Shiv helps kids to find their voices, dream up characters, and build entire worlds... out of (seemingly) nothing!

fighting-words.name: Fighting Words
fighting-words.bio: Fighting Words is a creative writing organisation established in 2009 by Roddy Doyle and Seán Love in Dublin. Our aim is to help students of all ages to develop their writing skills and to explore their love of writing. All programmes are free of charge and offered in locations all over Ireland. We offer a wide range of workshops, all of which are designed to promote creativity and writing as a fun and powerful means of self-expression. Join us for fun, creativity and sharing.

gsa-the-magic-of-disney.name: GSA - The Magic of Disney
gsa-the-magic-of-disney.bio: Let your little ones dive Under the Sea or step into the Circle of Life in this enchanting, interactive musical workshop. Packed with fun and magic, it’s the perfect experience for young Disney fans!

gsa-broadway-bites.name: GSA - Broadway Bites
gsa-broadway-bites.bio: Get ready to take a big Bite out of Broadway! From Hamilton to Sister Act—and, of course, the spellbinding WICKED!—this high-energy workshop brings the magic of musical theater to life.

school-fitness-ireland.name: School Fitness Ireland
school-fitness-ireland.bio: School Fitness Ireland is all about Making Fitness Fun. As Ireland's No.1 provider of PE coaches nationwide, trusted by over 900 principals they deliver workshops in Gymnastics, BoxAerobics, Fun Fitness and more

burning-circus-flow-artists.name: Burning Circus Flow Artists
burning-circus-flow-artists.bio: Burning Circus brings hoops, and playful movement to the Little Picnic. Blending rhythm, colour, and audience interaction into shows built especially for younger crowds. Expect juggling, hula hoop tricks, poi spinning, and plenty of laughs. Find them roaming Little Picnic with spinning, balancing, high energy, big smiles, and a genuinely joyful introduction to flow arts for the next generation of festival-goers.

the-bubble-guys.name: The Bubble Guys
the-bubble-guys.bio: The Bubble Guys are Ireland's premier bubble performance act, combining artistry, precision and playful interaction to create breathtaking large-scale soap bubble displays. Returning to Little Picnic, they will transform the festival landscape with enormous floating bubbles, intricate bubble garlands, shimmering webs and beautifully choreographed multi-string creations that drift effortlessly through the air. Their performances invite audiences to pause, look up and experience a moment of pure wonder. Blending visual theatre with spontaneous interaction, The Bubble Guys create an atmosphere that is both magical and joyful—equally captivating for young children, teenagers and adults alike. FREE unlimited sword balloons for children with every performance.

dj-sonic-boom-b2b-jammy-dodger.name: DJ Sonic Boom B2B Jammy Dodger
dj-sonic-boom-b2b-jammy-dodger.bio:
DJ Sonic Boom B2B Jammy Dodger is the sweet-and-sour collision you didn’t know your Electric Picnic needed.
Two selectors. One set. Absolutely no calorie counting.
Sonic Jam brings the rhythm, Jammy Dodger brings the filling, and somewhere in between the two lies a highly questionable but undeniably delicious journey through dancefloor favourites, forgotten gems, guilty pleasures and the occasional tune that has absolutely no business working until it does. A lot of the music comes directly from thrifted CD’s played live from a portable walkman…
It’s sweet. It’s sticky. It’s got a bit of crunch.
And once they’ve started, there’s no putting the packet back in the cupboard.

madonna-kebab.name: Madonna Kebab
madonna-kebab.bio:
Madonna Kebab is Cara Parc: performer, DJ, disco enthusiast and one of the wonderfully uncontainable forces behind Ireland’s Ping Pong Disco.
Born from DIY parties, queer club culture and a love of doing things just a little bit differently, Madonna Kebab brings together disco, house, camp, chaos and an infectious sense of fun. Her sets are less about behaving yourself and more about giving yourself permission to completely lose the run of yourself.
As part of the Ping Pong Disco family, she has helped create some of Ireland’s most joyful and outrageous festival experiences, spaces where disco bangers meet wild performance, glitter meets sweat and absolutely nobody is quite sure what’s going to happen next.
There’s a strong Irish streak running through it all: humour, mischief, irreverence and the ancient art of having the absolute craic.
Bring your dancing shoes. Leave your dignity at the door.

dj-battery-acid.name: DJ Battery Acid
dj-battery-acid.bio: DJ Battery Acid delivers the high-corrosive fuel needed to keep the festival pistons pumping. Expect a volatile cocktail of wonky techno, belligerent bass, and bombastic tekno, all heavily blessed with raw, chaotic Amen breaks. Pure high-voltage rave adrenaline designed for structural dancefloor damage.

donna-leake.name: Donna Leake
donna-leake.bio:
Global DJ and NTS Radio host of nine years, Donna Leake has also spent the last two years running three weekly shows on ROVR. Driven by an evolving love for sound exploration, her eclectic sets span global traditional folk, jazz, hip-hop, dub, UK bass, and cinematic library music.
Recently, Donna has injected heavier electronic sounds into her late-night club sets, diving deep into vinyl-only selections of dubstep, jungle, grime, dancehall, and experimental percussion.
Every performance adapts entirely to the venue, system, and crowd energy. Using music as a healer, teacher, and sonic portal, her ultimate mission is to craft a storytelling space where dancers can unite, reflect, and move freely through life's many moods together.

thxxti.name: THXXTI
thxxti.bio:
THXTTI is one of Dublin’s freshest young selectors, bringing a fearless, playful energy to the dancefloor and a serious instinct for knowing exactly what a crowd needs.
A regular around Dublin’s newest and most exciting club nights, THXTTI has appeared at Mo Cultivation, Club Comfort and Rathaus, quickly building a reputation as one to watch on the city’s underground circuit.
For this Metro set THXTTI has a one way ticket to bring Afro-electronic sounds to the platform.

dj-pcp-s-21st-century-carnival.name: DJ PCP's 21st Century Carnival
dj-pcp-s-21st-century-carnival.bio:
DJ PCP (Colm Olwill) is a riotous record obsessive hijacking the dancefloor since the early ’90s. Forget borders and genre rules—this set is a chaotic dive into rare, weaponized 21st-century carnival music.
As the mastermind behind Gramophone Disco, The Haunt, and Trad Rave, Colm has brought his sonic mayhem to Glastonbury, Electric Picnic, and All Together Now. Expect big beats, strange wax, and absolute musical anarchy.

fessa.name: Fessa
fessa.bio:
FESSA is a Berlin-based artist bringing a raw, unapologetic edge to the dancefloor. Born as a DIY solo project during lockdown, her sound lives somewhere between synth-punk, darkwave, electronic pop and the dirtier side of the underground.
Drawing on 80s-inspired bass loops, fuzzy guitars, distorted synths and infectious pop instincts, FESSA creates music that feels both nostalgic and completely of the moment. There’s darkness, humour, confrontation and plenty of attitude.
Her work refuses to sit neatly inside one genre, moving between driving electronic rhythms, post-punk energy and warped pop sensibilities. Recent appearances on underground European line-ups have seen her share space with artists from the techno, electronica and alternative scenes.
For Electric Picnic, expect something loud, strange and brilliantly unpredictable: dirty synths, heavy bass, punk spirit and enough attitude to shake the Metro out of its comfort zone.
FESSA doesn’t do background music.

gaff-e.name: Gaff-e
gaff-e.bio:
Gaff-e is mutating her signature, neon-drenched chaos into something far more sinister. Known across the global circuit for her wild energy and boundary-pushing showmanship, this specific outing sees her descending straight into the shadows.
Ditching the euphoric pop structures, Gaff-e is weaponizing a stark, late-night darkwave disco style set. Expect a hypnotic, pulse-pounding collision of industrial-tinged basslines, moody synthesizers, and bleak, driving electronic grooves. It’s gothic attitude meeting a sweaty dancefloor, dark, danceable, and a completely unpredictable DJ set you dont want to miss.

dj-b-augustus-b2b-milis.name: DJ B.Augustus B2B Milis
dj-b-augustus-b2b-milis.bio:
B.AUGUSTUS B2B Milis is a high-stakes meeting of underground tactical minds.
B.AUGUSTUS is a seasoned selector and Dundalk free-party veteran. He spent years hammering out blistering hard tekno with the DRATPAK sound system before anchoring the heavy, bass-driven hip-hop, reggae, and electronic rituals at the Spirit Store’s Backroom Bashment.
Flanking him is Milis, the rogue sonic architect and former core producer of the Tír na gCasta movement. For this collaborative assault, Milis isn’t just trading tracks, he has been deep in the trenches handling the underlying field research, mapping out a chaotic blueprint specifically tailored to maximize B.AUGUSTUS's explosive trajectory.

dj-dewalt-b2b-dj-hanibal-selector.name: DJ Dewalt B2B DJ Hanibal Selector
dj-dewalt-b2b-dj-hanibal-selector.bio:
DJ Dewalt is boarding a transatlantic flight very soon, trading Dublin build sites for big-money skyscraper contracts in New York. For his final Irish gig, he's bringing structural damage to your eardrums. Expect a wet mix of raw Irish trad, blistering hardcore, and jackhammer tempos. As his foreman noted: "His mixes have cracked more foundation walls than an earthquake. God Bless New York."
Flanking him for this Friday closing demolition is Hanibal Selector, the underground’s most elusive phantom. Rumored to be the main hitman and heavy fixer for the Dundalk TPM gang, Hanibal is a part-cartoon villain, part-evil genius who weaponizes bass like an acoustic mad scientist.

tailor-birds.name: Tailor Birds
tailor-birds.bio:
Tailor Birds is the dream-folk world of Sophie Kinston — a place where electric violin, live looping, vocals, spoken word and the sounds of the natural world collide.
At the heart of the project is a five-string electric violin, layered live with looping pedals, electronics and an ever-growing collection of sounds. Sophie’s music moves between folk, experimental electronics, classical textures and something altogether harder to name: music that feels like wandering through a strange forest at dusk.
Her fascination with the natural world goes even further. Through plant-music biosonification, electrical signals from plants, food, trees and even buildings can become part of the music, creating soundscapes that are genuinely rooted in their surroundings.
Sophie has spent years touring between Australia and Europe, appearing at festivals including Glastonbury, Vantastival, Rewild and Boyle Arts Festival. Now based in West Cork, she continues to create music that tells stories of love, loss, hope and possibility.
For the Metro, expect a little magic.

shelovescalpol.name: SheLovesCalpol
shelovescalpol.bio:
Over 20 years of friendship has led to this collaboration, creating bilingual lyrics and hip hop/trip hop beats with a twist of abstract echoing their sound system days. They have played at various venues & festivals since 2020, including Only Your Footprints, Body & Soul, Future Limerick, Fred Zeplins, Triskel Arts Centre, Brú Bar, Crane Lane, Electric Picnic 2023/2025,The Grand Social, Levis’s, Róisín Dubh
 and The Pav. They are currently working on their first album. You can find their tracks to date on Bandcamp. SLC have been played on Raidió na Gaeltachta and Raidió na Life.

na-dord-na-rialt-in.name: Na Dord & na Rialtáin
na-dord-na-rialt-in.bio:
“…Yet was it not my master to the very extent that it was my creature, had I not breathed into my own spirit” 

Colm Olwill(DJ PCP, Trad Rave) and well-known piper Eoin Ó Briain.

With a shared love of the pipes, the sesh and breakcore. Colm and Eoin met up to practice and explore how the sonorities of rave music can meld with the drones and tones of the Uilleann pipes. Bolting Irish and club music together to hear what monstrosities result.

dj-karmawi.name: DJ Karmawi
dj-karmawi.bio:
DJ Karmawi (the slang name for a rebel from Tulkarm, Palestine) is an Irish-Palestinian DJ and producer tearing up the rulebook. He doesn't just play tracks; he weaponizes the dancefloor as a portal into global lives and shared struggles.
Armed with a relentless passion for sonic expression, Karmawi hijacks Irish club culture to blast diverse electronic sounds from every corner of the underground. Expect heavy, driving basslines meant to make you groove and aggressive highs designed to make you move.
Pure solidarity, heavy frequencies, and absolute dancefloor liberation.

name: Лукас Огма
bio:
Лукас Огма, the Bruto Soviet Alter Ego of Lucas Ogma, Fuinneamh Festival founder, who takes us on a special journey curated especially for The Brutopolis State.
Since 2011, Lucas has been producing electronic music and DJing, crafting a richly textured, atmospheric, and hypnotic style of techno focused on stimulating raw emotion and guiding hypnotic dancefloor journeys.
This performance is a raw trip into post-Soviet times. It masterfully blends driving techno with post-punk industrial textures and retro synthwave. Think of this as a hot and sweaty Cold War music set.

magz.name: Magz
magz.bio: Magz has been deploying eclectic party bangers as weapons of mass disruption for the last decade. Not specific to one style but with an industrial, germanic and punk influence. She’ll be keeping it dark and dirty with a stomping set. No compromise, No regret, just relentless bangers

djackulate.name: DJackulate
djackulate.bio:
DJackulate is one of Ireland’s most distinctive turntablists, a Dublin-born musical polymath whose approach to DJing stretches far beyond the traditional decks. Also known as Jack Dempsey McMahon, he is a two-time world freestyle turntablist champion, renowned for his inventive use of samples, scratching and live manipulation.
A lifelong record obsessive, DJackulate digs deep into everything from Irish traditional music and folk to hip-hop, electronic music, jazz and experimental sounds, turning unexpected fragments into something entirely new. His work has seen him collaborate across the worlds of improvised music, theatre and electronic performance, while projects such as H-Ci and OKO showcase his restless, genre-defying approach.
He has also brought his unique take on Irish music to the dancefloor through Trad Rave, blending classic and contemporary trad with beats and bass alongside DJ PCP. 
Expect a set that refuses to stay on one track once the train leaves the Balkans.

dj-transit.name: DJ Transit
dj-transit.bio: Grab your whips and buckle up for one hell of a ride through the Wild Wild West—an afternoon of country classics, dusty trails and a fistful of country bangers.

strangelove.name: StrangeLove
strangelove.bio: Dundalk’s Laurence Kapinga, aka StrangeLove, has slowly been carving out a distinct space in Ireland’s music community as both a DJ and producer. With releases on 3024 and Reasons To Dance, as well as his work in the alternative R&B duo Negro Impacto, he’s become known for a sound that fluidly crosses genres while maintaining a singular identity within the Irish scene.

abha.name: Éabha
abha.bio:
ÉABHA is the electronic solo project of Éabha Campbell, known as a member of Irish post-punk outfit Madrúa. Based in Belfast, ÉABHA inhabits the darker, stranger edges of electronic music, pulling together industrial electronics, synth-pop, EBM, no-wave and post-punk into something both visceral and hypnotic.
There’s a beautifully unsettling quality to the project with detached vocals, pulsing electronics, cold synth textures and rhythms that seem to emerge from somewhere between a basement club and a dystopian nightclub. It’s music with atmosphere, attitude and a healthy disregard for genre boundaries.
Campbell’s background in sound-based performance and experimental art feeds directly into the project, where music becomes part of a wider world of texture, imagery and sensation.
For the Metro at Electric Picnic, expect something dark, physical and immersive. A set that shifts the temperature of the room and invites you into ÉABHA’s own electronic universe.

hykken.name: Hykken
hykken.bio:
HYYKEN is one of Ireland’s most exciting contemporary electronic artists, bringing a distinctly groove-led sound to dancefloors at home and far beyond. His music sits somewhere between stripped-back minimal house, rolling basslines, UK garage, techno and euphoric club energy, with a healthy dose of nostalgia running through it.
With releases on Patrick Topping’s Trick, DJ Haus’ UTTU, Southern Fried Records and Reboot Records, HYYKEN has developed a sound that manages to feel both underground and immediately infectious. His productions are built for movement, chunky grooves, memorable vocals, driving rhythms and those moments that turn a packed room into one big dancefloor.
His international journey has taken him from Irish festivals and clubs to Ibiza, Amsterdam, Bristol and Tenerife, including appearances alongside some of the biggest names in contemporary house music.
For the Metro at Electric Picnic, expect groove, nostalgia and serious dancefloor pressure. HYYKEN is here to get you moving, and he’s not planning on letting up.

influx.name: INFLUX
influx.bio:
INFLUX is an American electronic artist whose sound exists somewhere between the hypnotic, the psychedelic and the completely unexpected. A long-time explorer of the outer edges of electronic music, INFLUX moves effortlessly through acid, trance, techno, IDM and experimental sounds, creating sets that feel less like a DJ performance and more like stepping into another dimension.
There’s a distinctly old-school spirit running through the music with analogue textures, warped rhythms, hypnotic sequences and a fascination with the possibilities of machines. But INFLUX is never simply looking backwards. The sound is constantly mutating, pulling strange and unexpected influences into the mix.
INFLUX is for those who like their dance music a little stranger… Sound that gets under your skin, bends the edges of the room and keeps you up later than you should be.

azu-tiwaline.name: Azu Tiwaline
azu-tiwaline.bio:
Azu Tiwaline is a Tunisian producer and DJ whose hypnotic sound draws deeply from her Saharan roots and Tunisian heritage. Based between Tunisia and France, she creates an immersive meeting point between dub, techno, trance, experimental electronics and the raw, organic rhythms of North Africa.
Her music is shaped by the landscapes of El Djerid, incorporating field recordings, polyrhythmic percussion and deep bass into richly textured, psychedelic soundscapes. The result is both meditative and deeply physical — music that invites movement while creating a sense of place.
Azu has released acclaimed music through I.O.T Records and Bristol’s Livity Sound, including her albums Draw Me a Silence and The Fifth Dream. Her hybrid live/DJ sets have taken her to major festivals and clubs around the world, including Dekmantel, Dimensions, Freerotation, MUTEK, Unsound and Berghain.

backabeyond.name: BackaBeyond
backabeyond.bio: The Baka believe that "spirits" live in the forest who like to dance with people. Their music is designed to call these spirits to come and dance, and make peoples’ problems disappear. Festival favourites, Baka Beyond, certainly live up to this. With musicians from Cornwall, Wales, England, Congo and Sierra Leone, they mix the Spirit of the Forest with Celtic, African and modern sounds to create a positive feel-good vibe that you can’t help but move to. Let’s dance!

luke-thomas-and-paul-dunlem-big-band.name: Luke Thomas and Paul Dunlem Big Band
luke-thomas-and-paul-dunlem-big-band.bio: Ireland's KING OF SWING Luke Thomas and his band The Swing Cats - Specializing in uptempo swing music and VINTAGE POP MUSIC with two No.1 albums, Three TV Concerts Specials, countless sold out tours and 9 personally requested performances for President Higgins Luke Thomas & The Swing Cats are one of the most in-demand live bands in Ireland. As seen on Late Late Show, Ireland AM, SIX O'Clock Show, Today Show and heard on every major radio station in the country!!

the-circus-ponies.name: The Circus Ponies
the-circus-ponies.bio: Step into the mesmerising world of The Circus Ponies, a 16-piece band reimagining 90’s club classics with their own unique flair. Taking inspiration from Dec Pierce’s Block Rockin Beats, Jenny Greene and the Concert Orchestra & MEUTE, this musical collective delivers electrifying performances that have astounded audiences at venues and festivals across the country. Prepare for a dazzling visual and auditory feast as The Circus Ponies take the stage, igniting an explosion of colour, energy, and nostalgia. With their unstoppable presence and infectious beats, they bridge the gap between the past and the present, creating an unforgettable experience that will leave you yearning for more.

new-brass-kings.name: New Brass Kings
new-brass-kings.bio: The New Brass Kings is a 6-piece brass band from Dublin, Ireland. The band came together 8 years ago, finding common ground out of a love/hate relationship with brass, and music, and each other. The line-up of musicians differs here and there but fear not, the quality always stays at the highest level imaginable. Like, really imagine it. Often found busking in the centre of the city, they’re no strangers to festivals, parties, corporate functions, weddings, you name it.Thanks to the acoustic nature of the band and their mobility they’re easily the most versatile band in the entire world. Their setlist is comprised of the best songs you’ve ever heard, but played better, on brass. This is all sarcastic, please do not use it as a blurb for our gigs. We once played in a parade with an announcer who read this blurb to the whole crowd all the way to that last sentence before he realised what he had done. It was very funny.

los-wachos.name: Los Wachos
los-wachos.bio: Based in the vibrant city of Galway, Los Wachos is a spirited Latin band that celebrates the diverse sounds of Latin music. Our talented musicians hail from various countries, each bringing their unique flavour to our performances. As a close-knit group of friends, we share a passion for creating joyful, infectious rhythms that inspire everyone to hit the dance floor. We are on a mission to spread happiness through our music, touring across Ireland and lighting up pubs and festivals with our lively tunes. Join us for an evening of unforgettable fun, where our beats will surely make you move your feet!

tumbao-dublin.name: Tumbao Dublin
tumbao-dublin.bio: Nine salsa musicians. One mission: make you move. Tumbao Dublin brings the sounds of Cuba, Puerto Rico and Miami. Powered by deep hypnotic Afro-Cuban polyrhythms of rumba, punchy brass and groovy keys and tres cubano. The drums make you pound the ground. The Brass make you shimmy your shoulders ... and the bass ... that gets into your hips!!  Rooted in salsa tradition but played with the energy of a modern festival band, we bring azúcar, serious funk and even more serious sabor. . Electric Picnic — ¡a bailar!

largo-da-cumbia.name: Largo Da Cumbia
largo-da-cumbia.bio: Largo da Cumbia are on a mission to spread a message of unity through the rhythm of Latin America: Cumbia. With members from Chile, UK, and Portugal, each member brings a unique influence, mixing danceable grooves, psychedelic effects, and a Punk-Rock energy. The band has performed in Portugal, Spain, and Ireland, and they just released their debut EP that explores their roots of migration and cultural exchange. As musicians who have performed across Latin America and Europe, the band brings a unifying energy and positive vibes to each stage that never fails to get a crowd bouncing and turn casual crowds into committed Cumbia converts. The band creates a huge sound with only 5 members: effects pedals on Keyboard, Accordion and Clarinet meet the pounding groove foundation of Drums, Bass, Vocals and Guiro to bring audiences together dancing with an irresistible energy and message.

havana-roots.name: Havana Roots
havana-roots.bio: Havana Roots is a mash-up of traditional Son Cubano with the nearby Jamaican Reggae and Ska.

code-of-behaviour.name: Code of Behaviour
code-of-behaviour.bio: Code of Behaviour are an Irish brass band from Cork City. Their style is a blend of street jazz, jump-around pop and enough madness to make every moment a party. Originally known for "livening up the streets of Cork", the band features trumpets, trombones, mellophone, saxophone, sousaphone and drums, occasional vocals and – fortunately – just a little choreography. Get ready for mayhem.

sea-of-hope-choir.name: Sea of Hope Choir
sea-of-hope-choir.bio:
The Sea of Change is not your average choir. We’re a vibrant, mad craic, bunch of women brought together by cancer, friendship, music and a mad determination to enjoy life. We’ve featured on Ireland’s Got Talent, Britain’s Got Talent, we debuted at Electric Picnic last, recorded at Windmill Lane, received a standing ovation in European Parliament, Brussels for World Cancer Day, and sold our two concerts in the National Concert Hall

Out of a possible 120 boobs we have 109 and a half so if you see is dancing lopsided, bear with us.

Behind the sequins, singing and occasional chaos we fundraise through the incredible Strip & Dip, we have raised €1.5 million for Aoibheann’s Pink Tie, Ireland's Childhood cancer charity.  We are proud three-time Guinness World Record Holders.

We sing loudly, laugh even louder and believe life is for living. We are the Sea of Change – Come visit us

dj-harry-dj-o-kaye.name: DJ Harry & DJ O'Kaye
dj-harry-dj-o-kaye.bio:
O.KAYE is a London/Brighton-based DJ and selector, carving out a name with explosive energy behind the decks. Expect to be surprised and fully immersed: his performances seamlessly fuse hardgroove, breakbeat, underground rap, electro, jungle, and hardcore into a raw, high-energy force.

Founder of the rising event label All Be Equal (A.B.E.), O.KAYE has brought boundary-pushing parties to venues across the UK, with the collective now standing as a backbone of the London underground. 
He has lit up major festivals including Boomtown and Latitude, is part of the legendary Disco Shed, and has shared stages with icons such as Phil Hartnoll (Orbital), Hedex, Chamber 45, and many more.

Every performance is unpredictable and intense, a surge of rhythm and energy - built to move bodies, keep crowds locked in, and hit with bass that shakes sound systems to their core.

forro-dancers-tara.name: Forro Dancers & TARA
forro-dancers-tara.bio: Born in 2023, the Propaganda Van served as the Trailer Park headquarters for the highly incompetent festival political party, the Propaganda Machine, led by brutal dictator Naoise Ó Muirí. In 2023 he fought off democratic opposition to maintain power. In 2024, as the nation thrived, the ageing leader sought a successor from the festival crowd, but none would suffice. By 2025, other factions began to feel the power of the Propaganda Machine, and citizens rose in rebellion, led by Radio Providencia, who overthrew the regime—though Ó Muirí's fate remains uncertain. The shattered remnants of his party regrouped in Providencia, rebranding themselves as T.A.M.P.O.N.S.(Truthful Agenda Ministry of Powerful Organised National Socialists), However, beneath facade, their authoritarian nature lingered. As they resumed operations, Radio Providencia uncovered their deception, igniting a secret war of propaganda, mischief, and sabotage that spread throughout Providencia, 2025 in a chaotic clash of ideology and ego.

foreign-local.name: Foreign Local
foreign-local.bio: A duo with your eyes open but a full band with your eyes closed. Your best describing them yourself when you see and or hear them.

elise-frank.name: Elise FRANK
elise-frank.bio: French singer, guitarist and songwriter Elise FRANK blends Blues, Rock and Soul with a contemporary edge. Rooted in deep American blues and inspired by the raw energy of 90s garage rock, her music favours authenticity over polish. On stage, she performs with intensity and emotional depth, shaping a sound that is both direct and unfiltered. Following acclaimed appearances across Europe, including Ireland, the UK and major blues stages, and her signing with Ruf Records in 2025, Elise FRANK continues to build her presence on the European blues scene.

sally-cinnamon.name: Sally Cinnamon
sally-cinnamon.bio:
When a DJ has been at the helm of the party for 25 years, you know they’re doing something right. Sally Cinnamon exemplifies a golden age of the Irish party, which some may be too young to remember. For over two decades, she has been a mainstay in Irish nightlife institutions and now she’ll be performing at Beyond The Pale this weekend. 
You don’t have this much skin in the game without becoming a scholar of various sounds. The beautiful thing about a Sally Cinnamon set is that each one draws from a different world. Ranging from the psychedelic to the electronic to afro-sounds, no two sets are alike. A strong current of retro sounds run through her sets giving her selections the quality of unifying generations. 
There are two types of DJs, one that give an avalanche of bangers and ones that take you on a musical journey. Although Sally’s sets are far from devoid of stellar sounds, we’re also taken on an expedition, almost touching every continent with her selection. Nothing exemplifies this more than her Cabal, All aboard set. Skim through and you’ll be swung from jungle to italo-disco in a heartbeat, all whilst on a Viking ship. 
A DJ in their purest form, Sally Cinnamon is representative of a persistent culture of nightlife joy even against all the odds in Ireland.

gr-trad-session.name: Grá (Trad Session)
gr-trad-session.bio:
Grá are a 6 piece doom-folk project creating a new sound within the Irish folk scene, Grá combine acoustic and synthesised sounds that reimagine Ireland’s traditional music. 
Grá have captured a following early on that refuse to look away, the band host a weekly residency in Egan’s pub in Dublin.

morgana.name: Morgana
morgana.bio:
Fresh from RTE's Late Late Show, a special performance in an Amazonian Opera House, performing at Paris Fashion Week and opening for Snow Patrol on a series of massive outdoor shows this summer, Morgana’s momentum is undeniable. Before releasing any music she had already supported CMAT across North America and Europe and opened for Dermot Kennedy. Her recent single "I’m Not Going Anywhere" hit 100k streams in just two weeks and her Other Voices St James’ Church performance was selected for broadcast on BBC4, ahead of sold-out headline shows in Dublin and London. Her new single "Fix Your Heart For Free", out May 20th, sees Morgana flex her full vocal range as she showcases operatic vocal techniques over luscious indie pop instrumental.

Praised by Una Mullally in Irish Times as “a hugely sensitive performer… you can feel the 10,000 hours behind her,” Morgana brings a voice that stops rooms.

She first gained attention as a solo artist before co-founding Saint Sister, whose journey included opening for Robbie Williams, Keane, Tori Amos, Hozier and The National, plus a spellbinding NPR Tiny Desk Concert. With millions of streams and a devoted following, Morgana’s next chapter is a solo journey into kaleidoscopic popstar-dom. Her music is a mantra: prepared to party, ready to cry. Fans of CMAT, Kate Bush, Sharon Van Etten, and Chappell Roan will fall in love with Morgana’s technicoloured, tearful disco.

mo-cultivation.name: Mo Cultivation
mo-cultivation.bio:
The Mo Cultivation crew are bringing a feel good party to the Lovely Local on Friday evening. Packed with R&B, hiphop, soul, disco and 00s throwbacks... the kind of bangers you forgot you knew every word to, alongside gorgeous songs you might just be discovering for the first time.

Come with an open mind, stay for the great tunes and wonderful people. This music is for everyone, come enjoy yourself!

the-wran-trad-session.name: The Wran (Trad Session)
the-wran-trad-session.bio:
Hailing from the Comeragh Mountains of County Waterford, The Wran are four brothers: Tommy, Danny, Seán and Stephen Dunford. They bring a fresh voice to Irish music, blending trad with punk and a hint of psychedelia to create music that feels both timeless and new. Drawing inspiration from Planxty, The Pogues and Lankum,  
The Wran combines traditional and modern instrumentation, including banjo, harmonium, acoustic guitar, bass VI and drums. They are dedicated to keeping the Irish language, traditional songs and storytelling alive while continuing to push it forward in their own way.  
After an explosive live debut in 2025, including accoladed performances at Glastonbury, Green Man, All Together Now, and Electric Picnic, the band went on to support The Scratch and Kíla, play Dublin’s Notable NYD festival, and sell out their first Irish tour. Beginning 2026 with a sold-out UK tour, The Wran are fast establishing themselves as one of Ireland’s most vital new bands.

blkcnvs.name: BLKCNVS
blkcnvs.bio: BLKCNVS, the Dublin-based Nigerian-Irish DJ whose sets draw on a rich, global palette shaped by years of collecting and blending sounds across clubs, festivals, day parties, and even family gatherings. As founder of The Sweet Spot (@sweetspot.mp3), who currently host a monthly get together in Dublin City’s Project Arts Centre, he's focused on creating warm spaces that welcome dreamers & dancers to let loose, unwind & SHAKE RUMP — because it's good for you. Using riddims to spread much love from Ireland to The World.

surka.name: Surka
surka.bio:
Surka is a Dublin-based DJ, known for her distinctive house sound and instinctive approach to the dancefloor. In just three years, she’s taken her sound well beyond Ireland, with standout sets in London and Colombia and a Berlin debut at Renate. At home, she’s become a familiar name across the country’s biggest festivals, including Electric Picnic and All Together Now, and has shared lineups with Leftfield, Caribou and many more.

Her sets are confident, melodic and built around momentum, moving between deep and progressive house, trance and euphoric club music with a sound that’s distinctly her own.

A resident with Reclaim the Mainframe, Surka has established herself as one of the names to watch coming out of Dublin, with a growing international profile and an increasingly strong presence on the Irish festival and club circuit.

graham-smyth-b2b-claire-beck.name: Graham Smyth B2B Claire Beck
graham-smyth-b2b-claire-beck.bio:
Graham Smyth is a Broadcaster, Musician and DJ who you can catch both on-air on 2FM and at your local club or national festival. 
 
You might know 2FM’s Graham Smyth from presenting with Emma Power on Saturdays and 
Sundays. Or you might recognise him from his cover slots for Dave Fanning, Jenny Greene, Dan Hegarty and the like... Graham has on-air chats with the likes of Jungle, Erol Alkan and Jazzy as well as producing remixes for Irish artists such as Tolu Makay and Dark Tropics! 
 
Graham released his debut album, ‘Music For Babies To Rave And Sleep To’ via Practise Music in 2025, an ambient LP to introduce young ears to the soundscapes of electronic music. His live show in support of the album debuted at End Of The Road Festival in Dorset just before its release. 
 
As an in demand live DJ and as part of Dublin Record Club you can catch Graham spinning at 
Dublin venues like Fidelity, Lucky’s and The Devlin as well as at festivals such as All Together Now, Electric Picnic and Other Voices! With no restriction on genre but always an ear to the feet on the dancefloor (and a grá for an Irish tune), you can expect an eclectic set of records, no matter what type of set Graham is mixing! 

One of the most loved and sought-after DJs in Ireland, Claire Beck is a must-see fixture of Ireland’s
music festival and club scene. She is best known for award winning radio shows on TodayFM, and her joyful DJ sets where her signature style blends
House, Disco, Indie and Queer anthems designed to keep the dancefloor full.
Each performance is designed to tell a story, serving you music that you forgot you loved, music you
will love, with a sprinkling of spicy curveballs to keep you on your toes.

darren-regan.name: Darren Regan
darren-regan.bio: Darren Regan got into DJing as a teenager. He had a 3 year residency in his hometown in County Mayo while studying at Dublin City University. During his time in Dublin, he started to dabble in production and also began DJing at college events. After college he worked as a Host and Music Director on SPIN South West for a number of years while playing clubs and festivals across Ireland including Longitude and Electric Picnic.

little-o.name: Little O
little-o.bio: Little O is a DJ based in Dublin. Her sets are full of rhythmic and progressive sounds from around the globe. Expect to hear a blend of afrohouse, baile funk, batida, gqom, kuduro and more. A long term resident of Dublin Digital Radio, hosting and producing The Little O Show monthly on the digital station and is a regular on the Irish festival circuit, making appearances at All Together Now, Body & Soul, Electric Picnic, Haunted Dancehall and Open Ear. She has joined a great list of international acts on support duties including Ahadadream, Badsista, Brenda, C.Frim, DJ Danifox, Evehive and INVT.

and-he-the-fool-trad-session.name: and he, the fool (Trad Session)
and-he-the-fool-trad-session.bio:
and he, the fool are emerging as one of Ireland's most intriguing new bands, a seven headed entity with a sound that is ambitious, inviting and altogether distinctive. 

Hailing from all over the island and based between Dublin and London, their live show seamlessly shifts in style, perspective and language with a singular energy that holds crowds to every word and beat. 2025’s re:place the thought EP began to reflect this nature in their studio output, a record of moments confessional and raw. 2026 will see the release of some of their most hyped up tracks from their live performances to date, as well as a string of new gigs taking them across Ireland and

george-feely.name: George Feely
george-feely.bio:
Over the past number of years, George Feely has cemented himself as one of Ireland's most sought after party starters. With an upfront and energetic ethos, George's approach to music is that of a house purist, while also ensuring that everyone on the dancefloor is having a bloody good time!

With his early disco edits regularly appearing in the sets of industry leaders, George was handpicked by the German label Random Mind State for his first official release. With his debut record selling out in a matter of days, George went on to secure a string of successful EP's on powerhouse labels such as Unknown To The Unknown, Permanent Vacation, Nervous Records, Shall Not Fade, Edible, and Henry Street Music to name just a few.

dave-lofts.name: Dave Lofts
dave-lofts.bio:
With his raw, anthemic storytelling and indie-folk edge, Dave Lofts has drawn comparisons to a young Van Morrison and the soulful authenticity of Paolo Nutini. Through songs that feel deeply personal yet universally relatable, he has built a reputation for honest songwriting and captivating live performances, earning a fiercely loyal following both online and on stage. 
 
Dave’s story is as grounded as his music. A former member of the Irish Defence Forces, he brings a unique real-world perspective to his songwriting, adding depth and authenticity to his work. That connection with audiences is reflected not only in his rapidly growing streaming success — now surpassing 500,000 monthly listeners on Spotify — but also in his impressive live track record. He has sold out 25 consecutive Irish headline shows and completed a fully sold-out debut UK tour in April, including dates in London, Manchester and Glasgow. 
 
Earlier this year, Dave performed at the 20th Anniversary Oscar Wilde Awards in Los 
Angeles during Oscar Week, alongside Dermot Kennedy. The event honoured actor 
Domhnall Gleeson, and an impromptu performance of his latest single Holy with Sarenna 
Farrell generated over 10 million views across social media platforms. As a live performer, 
Dave has shared stages with artists including Gavin James, Wolf Alice, Picture This and Kingfishr, while standout appearances at Electric Picnic and All Together Now have further cemented his reputation as one of Ireland’s most exciting new talents.

minikimono.name: Minikimono
minikimono.bio:
A fixture in Ireland’s underground scene, Minikimono has spent the last 4 years curating dance floors that feel like home. With roots in promoting and party planning with her company H&G Creations she’s been shaping the sound and spirit of Irish nightlife for 18+ years — now channeling that same joyful community energy into her DJ sets.

Her sound moves between house, disco, and soulful grooves, blending warmth, rhythm, and emotional release. She curates her set to bring big energy, emotional storytelling and positive messages to uplift, energise and spread love to every person and every dance floor.

She’s played stages alongside Jungle and The Blessed Madonna, and performed at the likes of Electric Picnic (Smirnoff / Sound Nation), All Together Now, Beyond The Pale, Mother Club, and Love Tempo, among others.

At her core, Minikimono plays for connection — moments where strangers become friends, where joyful self expression feels inevitable.

esmeralda-road.name: Esmeralda Road
esmeralda-road.bio:
Esmeralda Road are a Belfast band quickly establishing themselves as one of the most exciting new live acts to emerge from the UK and Ireland.
Built on sharp songwriting, restless rhythms and an instinct for turning small rooms into full-blown parties, the band first gained attention through a string of sold-out shows in Belfast and early releases that spread quickly online. On stage, their reputation grew just as quickly. Esmeralda Road began taking their high-energy live show across the UK and Ireland, sharing stages with artists including Liam Gallagher and Primal Scream, while building a devoted following through touring.
Off the back of a support tour with Irish indie risers Basht., with new music on the horizon, and big live plans for the rest of the year, 2026 is shaping up to be a landmark year for Esmeralda Road.

jamie-mcintyre.name: Jamie McIntyre
jamie-mcintyre.bio: Galway songwriter Jamie McIntyre has enjoyed a breakthrough year, with his summer single “Over Galway Town” becoming a viral hit, amassing over 2.5 million Spotify streams and charting alongside some of the world’s biggest artists. The song’s success has carried his music far beyond Ireland and shows no signs of slowing. In 2024, McIntyre was hand-picked by Gavin James to support him in Paris on his European tour, leading to further opportunities including working with Imelda May and performing at Electric Picnic. He also joined Jamie Webster for sold-out shows in Dublin and Belfast. Momentum has continued into 2025, with McIntyre selling out his debut Irish tour in Dublin, Limerick, and Galway, before announcing larger shows for October. His recent EP, “Chapter 23”, has surpassed 750,000 streams, with tracks like “West Is Home” and “Grá” quickly becoming fan favourites.

shee.name: SHEE
shee.bio:
The luck of the Irish is no coincidence when it comes to David Sheerin aka SHEE.  
 
Playing his first DJ set aged 16, SHEE has spent near 10 years grafting and developing a fanbase on the Emerald Isle. Though these days, his sound is travelling much farther than that…  
 
Barry Can’t Swim, Fred again, Disclosure, salute and Mochakk are just a few names on the long list of SHEE’s supporters. His tracks have aired on Boiler Room, Cercle, Mixmag and more. While SHEE himself has gone from playing the Irish pubs in his local town, to packing out a 5k+ tent at All Together Now (Aug 2024), as well as supporting the likes of Bicep, Sofia Kourtesis, and Sally C.  
 
Outside of Ireland, SHEE has avid fans in Vancouver, London, Berlin and beyond, with recent appearances at Lost Village, Warehouse Project, Drumsheds and Amsterdam Dance Event. He heads into 2025 with big plans already - an Australian Tour in February (including plays at Lost Sundays and xe54 Club), a headline show at NTs Loft (London), a set with FLY in Edinburgh; plus support plays for Barry Can’t Swim in Sydney, Kettama at DEPOT Cardiff, and Laureunce Guy at Lakota, Bristol.  
 
His productions are also causing waves… ‘Win You Love’ (July 23) tallies over 4.4mil streams on Spotify and features in the EA Formula 1 video game. But this momentum suggests that SHEE’s next releases will set new levels. All his releases in 2024 featured in New Music Friday UK, and his most recent single ‘LEAVES’ landed with playlist cover of Breakthrough Electronic on Amazon Music. More works in progress with Denis Sulta, Sam Alfred, Laurence Guy mean that SHEE’s sound will become ever more unavoidable.

newdad.name: NewDad
newdad.bio:
Life is all about balance, and for every dream experience that shakes up your world, there’s often a sacrifice to be made. NewDad have had plenty of the former since releasing their debut single ‘How’ in 2020 and steadily building an ever-burgeoning fanbase around their spellbinding dream-pop. They’ve released a critically-acclaimed debut album in 2024’s ‘Madra’, gained a fan in their ultimate hero, The Cure’s Robert Smith, and toured parts of the world they never thought they’d get to visit. But for all that to be possible, the Galway three-piece have had to give up some things, too.  
 
Around four years ago, the band – singer/guitarist Julie Dawson, guitarist Sean O’Dowd, drummer Fiachra Parslow – left their home behind and moved to London. It’s a relocation that’s helped them thrive as a group, but is also something that Dawson still has mixed feelings about. “Most days I wake up and I’m like, ‘Yes, let’s fucking do this’, but I do still miss home,” she explains.  
 
That tension between knowing you’re where you need to be right now and longing to be somewhere else colours ‘Altar’, NewDad’s highly anticipated second album. Started shortly before the release of ‘Madra’, it’s deeply informed by Dawson’s yearning for home, for family and the place that she truly belongs. In some ways, the record is a tribute to Galway, the singer in reverence of her hometown.  
 
“The album itself is where I divulge my love for home,” Dawson shares, nodding to its title. “It’s the idea that Ireland is the altar and it’s the thing that I worship, in a way.” The meaning that imagined altar takes on has multiple layers to it, too. It’s a reference to the sacrifice the band has made in putting hundreds of miles between them and the people they cherish most – “Sacrifice is another thing that happens at altars; I haven’t seen it, but I’ve heard that happens,” Dawson laughs. ‘Altar’ also taps into some of the themes in the lyrics of “appeasing people, and that’s what you do at altars – appease a higher power”.  
 
“I think of where / I’d like to be / Anywhere but here / Is fine by me,” Dawson sings on the twinkling slow build of opening track, ‘Other Side’. Across that song and the album in general, that burning for home – for the place Dawson feels most at ease and like her true self – grow darker and more anxiety-ridden, themes of survival and needing to be saved repeatedly piercing through. “Kneeling at the altar / Hope I get to heaven,” she sighs on ‘Mr Cold Embrace’, an acoustic-guitar-led, string-laden beauty that also finds the singer questioning “don’t know if I should have left her”.  
 
‘Misery’, meanwhile, finds her interrogating her role in her unhappiness, acknowledging the sometimes self-inflicted nature of her gloom. “It’s all these cyclical things that we do and these patterns we fall in and out of,” she explains. “I was like, ‘Can I go home? Do I need to be here? Why am I doing this to myself? Why am I putting myself in these situations where I’m becoming deeply unhappy?’” Dawson wanted to make the song sound “surreal and alarming”, inspired by the imagery in Dante’s Inferno. “It’s very whispery and freaky.”  
 
Finale ‘Something Broken’, though, breaks the dwelling and yearning, Dawson asking to feel at home in her current location, to laugh harder, to forget what’s tormenting her. “It’s a more hopeful message in that it’s like, ‘I’m here now, let’s make the best of something that can be really hard’,” she says.  
 
‘Altar’ – recorded in January 2025 between studios in Ipswich and London – isn’t simply an album about where one comes from and wants to get back to, though. It also charts Dawson’s journey as a musician, coming to terms with the realities of her hobby and passion becoming a profession, and navigating the industry as a woman. “When you start doing music, you do it because you love playing music, you love making music,” she reasons. “I hadn’t really considered the other aspects – touring is so fun, but it’s intensive. It’s difficult. Doing social media, I hate it. Just a lot of inside pressures and politics – it’s a lot more pressure than I thought it would be.”  
 
Music, though, is still the outlet Dawson uses to alleviate the stresses in her life – even when they come from music itself. You can tell how impactful songwriting is for her just by looking at her catalogue of work so far – and the prolific levels at which she writes. ‘Altar’ was written before NewDad’s debut album had even been released, and between that record and this, she found the time to release her first solo album, ‘Bottom Of The Pool’, too.  
 
Across all of her writing, but particularly on ‘Altar’, her artistry has helped her to find more understanding of both who she is as a person and her relationship with being a musician. “These songs have definitely helped me understand that and become a stronger person,” she nods. “I can be bad at standing up for myself. But you really need to do that in music, otherwise people will take the piss. I definitely realised that through songwriting.” 
 
That side of ‘Altar’ finds the singer grappling with her people-pleasing tendencies on ‘Entertainer’ and tackling the expectations put on female musicians on ‘Heavyweight’. 
‘Roobosh’, a tightly-wound song that’s driven by a propulsive, rumbling bassline and Dawson’s sudden yells, plunges us into the confusing quagmire of being a woman in society, pulled deeper and deeper down by the expectation to be “so patient and understanding and nice all the time”.  
 
“That is placed on us, but I also definitely play into that,” Dawson explains. “I’m a people pleaser, and I’m trying not to be, but I want to make people happy. I just wanted to have one song where I just went, ‘Fuck you, fuck this’. I wanted to just have a whinge and one song where I just fucking went for it. I wanted it to be slap bang in the middle of the record, just completely off-kilter, like, ‘What the fuck?’” 
 
For NeFittingly, given the love for home on ‘Altar’, the continued ascent of the three-piece on this record will also continue to further Ireland’s current standing as a hotbed of world-beating creative talent. NewDad are bringing something fresh to the new wave of original, formidable young acts from the country, distinctive from their peers as they join them in making waves around the world.  
 
Whether live or on record and regardless of where listeners are tuning in from, Dawson hopes ‘Altar’ helps people gain the courage to stand up for themselves and be proud of themselves, and gain the strength that this confident new album has given her. “Nothing’s perfect,” she reflects, “but if you just work hard and are true to yourself, it’ll be alright.” Sacrifices might still have to be made in the balancing act of life, but ‘Altar’ at least has helped Dawson accept that and is about to take NewDad to even greater heights.  wDad’s second album, the band enlisted rising producer Shrink – aka Sam Breathwick – to work with them in the studio, as well as reuniting with writer Justin Parker. The relationship with Shrink began in writing sessions, coming up with ‘Entertainer’ and ‘Safe’, the title track from the band’s 2025 EP, together. “These songs that we spent two days writing and he produced sounded perfect, so I was like, ‘I want to see what else we can do’.”  
   
The results are a record that’s as beautiful as it is crunchy and in-your-face, deftly skipping between sparkling, gentle moments and heavy blasts of guitar and bass whenever the songs demand. It’s more pop-leaning in its scope, drawing from Dawson’s appreciation of the current pop landscape and “cool rock bands with a lot of brightness to them” like R.E.M. and The Sundays.  
 
The expansion of the NewDad sound will be reflected in the band’s new live show – an already acclaimed setup that’s gained them slots at every major UK festival, landed them support slots for Pixies, Fontaines DC and The War On Drugs, and taken them as far afield as Japan and China. “I think our biggest headline show was in Shanghai, and the whole crowd were singing ‘White Ribbons’,” Dawson recalls. “I burst into tears. That’s the only time that’s ever happened to me, but I was like, ‘How is this real?’”  
 
The next phase of NewDad touring – which sees them return to China, Japan, North America, Europe and the UK over the rest of 2025 – will see Shrink join their on-stage line-up too. His addition will, Dawson says, make the songs sound “much more full”: “It’s a big step up. The songs that we have struggled with before – getting them across live – we have that now because we have another person.”  
 
Fittingly, given the love for home on ‘Altar’, the continued ascent of the three-piece on this record will also continue to further Ireland’s current standing as a hotbed of world-beating creative talent. NewDad are bringing something fresh to the new wave of original, formidable young acts from the country, distinctive from their peers as they join them in making waves around the world.  
 
Whether live or on record and regardless of where listeners are tuning in from, Dawson hopes ‘Altar’ helps people gain the courage to stand up for themselves and be proud of themselves, and gain the strength that this confident new album has given her. “Nothing’s perfect,” she reflects, “but if you just work hard and are true to yourself, it’ll be alright.” Sacrifices might still have to be made in the balancing act of life, but ‘Altar’ at least has helped Dawson accept that and is about to take NewDad to even greater heights.

brooki.name: Brooki
brooki.bio: BROOKI are a four piece band from Dublin, Ireland, blending raw emotion with atmospheric guitars, heavy rhythms and infectious melodies. Drawing comparisons to the emotional honesty of Jeff Buckley and the grit of early PJ Harvey, the band create a sound that is both intimate and cinematic. Moving between moments of restraint and explosive intensity. Driven by distorted guitars, bass-heavy textures and dynamic live energy, BROOKI’s sound is anchored by Sarah’s striking vocal performance, which cuts effortlessly through the noise. With emotionally charged songwriting and powerful live performances, BROOKI leave a lasting impression long after the final note fades.

big-sleep.name: Big Sleep
big-sleep.bio: Big Sleep are a Dublin-based rock band making their name the old-fashioned way; through tireless gigging and a shared passion for live performance. From underground tunnel shows beneath the M50 to sold-out European tours, their journey is one of instinct, connection, and constant evolution. Formed by lead vocalist Rónán Connolly and Italian drummer Matteo Poli, the band later solidified with bassist Aidan Gray and guitarist Naiara Clarke LaFuente, who joined after a chance encounter involving an illegal rave, a forest, and a homemade stage. Their debut album ‘Holy Show’ is a conceptually rich and emotionally vulnerable collection that explores love, loss, and identity. In Ireland, a “holy show” refers to a messy situation, and each of the album’s ten tracks delves into its own emotional chaos.

sarah-crean.name: Sarah Crean
sarah-crean.bio:
Sarah Crean is an Irish singer-songwriter and producer based in Brighton. Her sharp eye for life’s intimate details and moreish voice shine through her dreamy, slow-burn Indie Pop. 

With a fast-rising catalogue including her 2023 EP Death by Laundry, home to viral single “02:00 am” (20M+ streams) and widespread international support, Crean has become unstoppable. Recent singles ‘22 Angel’ and ‘Baby (I'll Always Be the Lead)’ have continued that momentum, landing on Spotify's New Pop UK and marking Crean's first releases returned as a fully independent artist. 

Fresh off SXSW Austin, Crean is now on the cusp of releasing her sophomore album, Heirloom - entirely made by women. Sarah Crean has toured extensively with the likes of Florence Road, Bombay Bicycle Club, Pillow Queens, Haley Blais, U.S. Girls and more, and played standout shows including opening for Blackpink in Hyde Park and CMAT at London's O2 Forum Kentish Town.

le-boom.name: Le Boom
le-boom.bio:
Le Boom are Irish brothers Andy and Christy Leech, an electronic act known for their immersive live shows that sit somewhere between a gig, a rave and a house party. 
 
Instead of performing on a stage, they play from the floor in the middle of the room, surrounded by the crowd. With Christy and Peter Fleming building the music live and Andy’s spoken word cutting through the tracks, the audience becomes part of the show rather than just watching it. 
 
Over the past two years, Le Boom have built a loyal grassroots following through their secret Gael Rave events and dedicated WhatsApp communities. What began as a handful of intimate nights has grown into a community spanning Ireland, the UK, Australia and New Zealand, with pop-up events in Glasgow, Liverpool, London and beyond. 
 
Musically, Le Boom draw as much from trad, indie and spoken word as they do from electronic music. Their songs move naturally between Irish and English, reflecting the bilingual community that’s grown around the band.

f3miii.name: F3miii
f3miii.bio:
F3miii is an Irish singer, songwriter and producer creating a distinctive blend of alternative R&B, electronic music and soulful songwriting. Known for his cinematic production and emotionally honest lyricism, he has quickly become one of Ireland's most exciting new artists. 
 
Over the years, F3miii has received support from many publications including; BBC, RTÉ and Hot Press. No stranger to the big stage either, having performed at international festivals including Forbidden Fruit and Electric Picnic.  
 
F3miii reached an international breakthrough in 2026 with his hit single "Noble." The track has since amassed over 100 million Spotify streams, charted across multiple countries and earned him his first appearance on the Billboard Hot 100 - making him the first solo Black Irish artist to achieve the milestone.

cruel-sister.name: Cruel Sister
cruel-sister.bio: Fresh from supporting Wet Leg in Dublin & Just Mustard across their UK tour, Cruel Sister quickly emerges as one of the most exciting voices in Ireland's alternative scene. A self-produced force within the new wave of shoe gaze, and alternative rock, her live show is massive, where delicate vocals hang in suspension against unrelenting guitar distortion. Her 2025 EP A CORPSE IS TALKING, featuring 6 Music favourites IRON PILLS and WINDOW SEAT, received the support of The Irish Times, NME, Clash, DIY, Wonderland, Notion, The Line of Best Fit, 1883 Magazine, District Magazine, The Forty-Five, Hot Press and Nialler9.

sell-everything.name: SELL EVERYTHING
sell-everything.bio:
SELL EVERYTHING. Rooted in Dublin city’s DIY music scene and shaped by late-night sessions, worn-out tape decks, and a deep love for raw, honest songwriting. Formed in 2023, the group is led by frontman, guitarist, and songwriter Tom Kelly, whose creative vision drives their music, visual art, and clothing projects. He collaborates closely with lead guitarist Jack Usher, bassist Fionn Mac Lochlainn and drummer Oisín Cavanagh— a group of multi-instrumentalists, songwriters and producers. Also including Toby Whelan, a wizard on the modular synth. He adds a soundscape of dub delays and sirens which act as the glue that hold the band together.
With influences like King Krule, Toro y Moi, and Bar Italia, SELL EVERYTHING blends swirling textures with off-kilter grooves to create music that feels both intimate and expansive. Their tracks have landed on major Spotify playlists, including Pollen and Fresh Finds UK & Ireland, connecting with a growing audience of psychedelic and indie fans worldwide.

anna-leah.name: Anna Leah
anna-leah.bio:
anna leah is an indie artist and singer-songwriter from Dublin. The solo artist blends folk elements with indie rock vibes, dreamy pop, and stripped-back acoustic sounds to create her musical style. Through her masterful songwriting and honey toned vocals front and centre, Anna invites her listeners on a relatable and poignant journey through themes of nostalgia, self-discovery, and navigating her coming-of-age journey, solidifying anna leah's status as an artist to watch in 2026 and beyond.

She has featured on some impressive lineups such as All Together Now Festival, Other Voices, Ireland Music Week, The Ruby Sessions and has opened for Sombr, Florence Road, James Vincent McMorrow, jasmine.4.t and Nell Mescal. Finding influence in her favorite artists such as Beabadoobee, Lizzy McAlpine, Phoebe Bridgers and everyone in between.

aifric.name: Aifric
aifric.bio:
Aifric is a singer and songwriter from Galway whose music feels driven by something elemental – a kind of creative and emotional exorcism she describes as “holding a ball of fire that wants to be thrown somewhere.”
Raised in the rugged west of Ireland, immersed in the Irish language and a strong storytelling tradition, Aifric’s musical instincts took shape early. She began singing at an Irish-speaking convent school in Dingle, and later lived between a caravan on a dairy farm, a narrowboat in London, and an old grain mill in East Galway.
It was at the mill, that writing became the way she steadied herself. Songwriting that explored the complexities and richness of ordinary life, the beauty and brutality of landscape, the shifting identities of girlhood and adulthood, and a quiet resistance to the noise of modern culture.

sally-c.name: Sally C
sally-c.bio:
Whether via her DJ sets or label Big Saldo’s Chunkers, Sally C has developed one of the most distinctive sonic signatures in electronic music. The Belfast-born, Berlin-based artist traverses the gamut of vintage house, hip house, acid and breakbeat, all with that unmistakable Chunker sound. 
 
Sally’s DJing journey begun in 2010 at the Reading Rooms in Dundee, Scotland, an iconic local club, playing host to the likes of DJ Pierre, DJ Sneak and Green Velvet. It was here she met an open-minded and accepting community and gained a crucial education in digging, mixing and all things dance music culture, an experience that would set her up for the rest of her career.  
 
These guiding principles of authenticity, community and independence lie at the core of who Sally is as an artist and have defined her brick-by-brick journey since day one. Moving to Berlin in 2015, she etched out a spot in the city’s thriving club scene, throwing parties at Griessmühle and her own open-air raves, all the while building a fanbase for her raw and chunky style. When she was tapped for her debut Boiler Room in 2019 at AVA Festival, it was a noticeable levelling up. No longer a developing talent, RA lauded her as a festival highlight, noting her “musical range and technical acuity”.

cardinals.name: Cardinals
cardinals.bio:
From a small, dark room on the northside of Cork city - a rehearsal space that is “very cold in the winter and very hot in the summer” - Cardinals have emerged with a debut album that appropriately swings from one extreme to the other. Darkness to light. Light to darkness. Hopefulness to despair. Compassion to chaotic indifference. 
 
A band forged through both family and friendship - brothers Euan (vocals, guitar) and Finn (accordion) Manning, their cousin Darragh (drums, tambourine, glockenspiel) and their former schoolmates Oskar Gudinovic (guitar) and Aaron Hurley (bass) - the five-piece have already positioned themselves at the vanguard of the Irish independent rock scene. And with Masquerade, they have flung off the shackles of their early influences to craft something entirely their own.  
 
“This feels like a natural progression,” says frontman Euan. “The early years feel like a band still finding ourselves and trying different things. 
Whereas the album's a bit more cohesive and a little bit more sure of itself.” 
 
Euan’s description of these songs as “soft ballads whipped into urgency out of a panicked necessity” aptly captures Masquerade’s mood; these are emotionally expansive songs, some simmering with an undercurrent of violence, cynicism or fervent discontent (Anhedonia, The Burning of Cork, Barbed Wire) others gleaming with a bright-eyed vulnerability. Crafting a record with an A-side and a B-side is a nod to the band’s collective love of vinyl, and Masquerade’s tonal shift takes its cue from a variety of contrasting influences - from Townes Van Zandt’s “soft and beautiful melodies” to heavier fare like Nine Inch Nails, Danish punks Iceage and goth-metal icons Type O Negative, as well as their previously-noted love of hip-hop. 
 
“For the most part, the B-side is a darker and grittier exploration of the themes than what comes before,” explains Euan. “I always appreciated it when a record could have that juxtaposition. Bowie's Low comes to mind; to have Warszawa on the same record as Be My Wife is brilliant. 
Sometimes an artist might be made to feel like they should write something that works and then reproduce it as many times as they can for the record, but exploring and experiencing different states of emotion is a human thing. 
That's something that interested us when it came to making this record.” 
 
Recording the album without a click track proved crucial to capturing the “beautifully imperfect” sound of Masquerade. With most songs written over the past 18 months, the band recorded in the legendary RAK Studios in London, with their fellow twentysomething producer Shrink at the helm. Studio engineer Isabel Gracefield suggested that Euan record his vocals for As I Breathe in the studio’s stairwell, which further stripped back the singer’s defences. 
 
“Office workers in RAK would descend the stairs after their day’s work and I'd greet them with a full mic setup,” he recalls, smiling. “It was a jarring experience, at first. Feeling scrutinised by the band or producer is usually enough to throw me off, so with strangers it was a whole other experience. But eventually you just let go and fight through it. And the end result is a take we were very happy with.” He nods. “Its vulnerability occurred in real time, as the song was laid down.” 
 
When it comes to lyrics, Euan is conscious of leaving songs open to the listener’s interpretation. He rails against the idea of songs having to be borne from personal experience, describing it as ‘reductive’ to assume that songwriters cannot write from a place of fiction or imagination, like any other writer. “I wish that my life was as interesting or as romantic as some of the songs make it out to be,” he laughs. “But a lot of them are just stories.” 
 
One real world element that did unintentionally become a running theme on the album was the multitude of religious references littered throughout Euan’s lyric sheet, whether it’s “Bask in the relief/ At the throne of Jesus Christ” on She Makes Me Real, “Don’t you think I’m holy? / The way the cross is on my neck” on Over at Last, or As I Breathe’s “You can wear the chain, I'll wear the collar of my clerical order”. 
 
“We all probably have different ideas individually of what our faith might be - but I think we're all really interested in the beauty of churches and religious symbolism, and stained glass,” says Finn. “I do think we all have some form of faith on the spectrum somewhere. I think the shift from a seriously Catholic country to a fairly secular country after the Murphy Report in 2009 probably had an effect, as well. Big social changes that happen when you're a child do affect you more than you realise.” 
 
Euan nods. “I try not to look too closely at what it is or why it appears so much in my songwriting,” he shrugs, “but it's there, and we're definitely connected to it - whether we like it or not.” 
 
There are other subtle nods to real life, whether drawn from personal experience or not. Cardinals rebuff the notion of being branded as a “Cork band” or even an ‘Irish band”, shirking off the ‘fetishisation’ of Irish culture that is being brazenly embraced by other acts and embellished by certain factions of the media. Nevertheless, their adopted city is in their creative DNA. The ferocious jolt of Anhedonia was inspired by a violent incident that Euan witnessed not long after moving to the city from the band’s hometown of Kinsale. Barbed Wire, with its lyric “Alcohol and ecstasy / And Aperol and THC / From City Hall / To George's Quay” was partly inspired by the acclaimed Irish writer Kevin Barry’s work, notably an essay that he wrote about his time in Cork. The Burning of Cork is an inadvertent protest song of-sorts, which draws parallels between the ongoing genocide in Gaza and the British forces’ decimation of Cork in 1920, as the lyrics despair at the patterns of violence repeated “again and again and again.” 
 
Other external touchpoints include the band’s discovery of the work of 
Norwegian-Irish artist Oda Sønderland. Her painting Fristeren was formative in creating the world of the record and shaping its themes, and which now graces the cover of Masquerade.  
 
“It’s such a striking image: it's like a refuge in what is otherwise a harsh and cold environment,” says Euan. “When I think of listening to records, or watching movies or art in any way, that's the way that I see it; as this place of refuge and intimacy. I think we all fell in love with that piece. It’s completely beautiful. And I think we just kind of knew that it had to be the cover.” 
 
It’s clear that Masquerade marks a new era for Cardinals. The making of the album has revealed something new of themselves, opening them up as a more collaborative entity - as evidenced by closing track As I Breathe, written just one week before they entered the studio. While much of the record’s lyrical content deals with the trials and complexities of navigating life, the album ends on a tentatively hopeful note with the striking line “Even as we fall / I have learned the world is small / And I proceed.” 
 
“I think you can definitely put the emphasis on ‘band’ now more than ever, for the five of us as a working unit,” nods Euan. “The first album is daunting, but I feel like you’re not going to look at anything the same afterwards, artistically. The work that goes into it is an awful lot, and you're putting a lot on the line in terms of vulnerability and opening ourselves up, emotionally.” He sighs softly, smiling. “It'll change whatever we decide to do next, musically or otherwise. I think it'll have that effect on all of us.”

black-nylon.name: Black Nylon
black-nylon.bio:
Formed in 2025 from the debris of initial musical projects and a collective need to create something fresh, black nylon bring a polarising yet deeply emotive sound that feels distinctly authentic. Warped by sonic shimmers and fuelled with a heavy rhythm section, even their earliest work feels timeless, with their live performances carrying an unwavering, effortless cool.  
 
From supporting the likes of Inhaler, Bleach9:3, THEATRE and Kneecap to selling out London’s ‘Third Man’ and securing coveted slots at All Together Now and Electric Picnic, black nylon have proved their place as pioneers of the new generation of alternative music from the outset. Now with a weekly DJ set at the well-known Workman’s Club in Dublin and a headline show at Camden’s Elephants Head booked with So Young for September, black nylon’s versatility and growing live presence has already named them “Dublin noisemakers” (Hot Press).

tooth.name: Tooth
tooth.bio:
Over the last year, the quartet - comprised of Tom Pollock (guitar, vocals), Ben Ashley (guitar), Charlie Arnison (bass) and Roy Lowe (drums) - have meticulously honed their craft, becoming one of the most talked-about new bands in the country for their riotous live shows which fuse anthemic US alternative, second-wave emo and garage rock. 
 
Building a devoted live following for a show that’s well-drilled yet off-kilter, as prone to erratic, noisy breakdowns as it is to shout-along choruses, they've racked up an impressive resumé that’s seen them open for the likes of Keo and Sunny Day Real Estate and hit up festivals including Live At Leeds, Sŵn, Mutations, Kendall Calling and Tenement Trail.

burglar.name: Burglar
burglar.bio:
Burglar is an alternative rock band based in Dublin, Ireland. Willow and Eduardo formed Burglar after meeting in college in 2021 and bonding over their love of alternative acts such as Stereolab and Smashing Pumpkins. Their backgrounds couldn’t be more different; Eduardo grew up around the punk rock scene in his hometown of Goiânia, Brazil, while Willow comes from the indie-pop scene in Dublin. However, their blend of inspirations has given Burglar a unique and addictive sound. Willow’s dissociative lyricism and Eduardo’s confessional style result in energetic and catchy songs with interchangeable vocal leads and omnipresent harmonic work, alongside distorted guitars and buzzing synths.
 
They’ve been a mainstay of the Dublin gig scene for the last few years. Following their much-anticipated showcase at Ireland Music Week in 2024, they have gone from strength to strength, selling out their first two headline shows in Dublin, and completing support tours with US Girls, Adore, The Belair LipBombs and Theatre Band. Their own headline shows saw them playing in iconic London venues such as Windmill Brixton and Moth Club. They marked 2026 as their breakout year with the release of the absolute ear-worm 'Lovey' in January, closely followed by being named as one of The Irish Times 50 people to Watch for 2026. They've toured Bristol, Manchester, Glasgow and Leeds with their most recent single 'Star-Crossed', also winning over new fans at this year's The Great Escape, Brighton. They're now working on their debut album.
